jobs.title: Engineering Intern, SRE
jobs.description:
ONWARDS TOGETHER!

Illumio is the leader in ransomware and breach containment, redefining how organizations contain cyberattacks and enable operational resilience. Powered by the Illumio AI Security Graph, our breach containment platform identifies and contains threats across hybrid multi-cloud environments – stopping the spread of attacks before they become disasters.

Recognized as a Leader in the Forrester Wave™ for Microsegmentation, Illumio enables Zero Trust, strengthening cyber resilience for the infrastructure, systems, and organizations that keep the world running.


THIS IS A 12 WEEK INTERNSHIP PROGRAM BEGINNING ON MAY 24TH 2027 OR JUNE 21ST 2027

 


LOCATION: 4 ON-SITE DAYS A WEEK IN SUNNYVALE, CA HEADQUARTERS.




OUR TEAM'S VISION:

Our Engineering team has established a culture based on thought leadership, independence, and responsibility. This powerful dynamic drives us forward as we work to make the digital world a safer place.    
 
Those who join us represent the leader in Zero Trust Segmentation and work on a technology stack that ranges from operating systems to distributed applications to UI and visualization. Together, we will continue to build world-class products—driven by people with different perspectives, backgrounds, and a commitment to innovation in a time when the world faces its greatest cybersecurity threats in history.  



YOUR IMPACT:

 - Gain hands-on expertise in public cloud infrastructure management and deployment in Kubernetes

 - Participate in projects to integrate AI services into existing workflows 

 - Learn to implement and optimize monitoring public cloud ecosystems for efficient system health tracking and Observability

 - Acquire practical skills in building, managing and optimizing CI/CD pipelines for applications

 - Enhance troubleshooting skills, focusing on diagnosing and resolving issues in cloud-native and distributed systems 

 - Develop proficiency in designing for scalability to support growing data and workloads

 - Master modern deployment practices, ensuring reliable and efficient releases
   
   


YOUR TOOLKIT:

 - Currently enrolled in a full-time Bachelor's or Master's degree-seeking program with an expected graduation date in Winter 2026/Spring 2027

 - Good understanding of object-oriented programming, data structures and algorithms including distributed systems 

 - Proficiency in C++/Python/Go, or similar programming language and willingness to learn Go language quickly 

 - Experience with AI tools/models and AWS/Azure working experience a plus

 - Examples of your own self-driven projects that illustrate your passion for software development 
   
   


WHAT YOU’LL GAIN:

 - Hands-on experience running and scaling production cloud infrastructure that supports Illumio's Zero Trust Segmentation platform

 - Real-world experience with Kubernetes, public cloud platforms (AWS/Azure), and modern CI/CD and deployment tools

 - A look at how observability, monitoring and incident troubleshooting keep distributed systems reliable at scale

 - Experience bringing AI services into real engineering workflows, a skill more and more companies are looking for

 - Mentorship from experienced Site Reliability and Cloud Engineers and technical leaders

 - A better understanding of how reliability, scalability and security are built into a cybersecurity product from code to release
   
   

A supportive and inclusive environment that values curiosity, ownership and continuous learning

To support you throughout your internship, Illumio interns can look forward to:

 - Stipend: A stipend to help support you during your internship.

 - Events & Experiences: Fun and meaningful events providing opportunities to connect with fellow Illumineers to build new skills and experience our culture.

 - Giving Back: Opportunities to volunteer and make an impact in our community.

 - Meals & Snacks: Stay fueled with a fully stocked office, snacks and beverages, plus catered lunch from local restaurants every day!
   
    

#LI-PO1 #LI-ONSITE

 

Candidates selected for an internship must have valid U.S. work authorization for the full duration of the internship. Illumio does not provide immigration sponsorship for internship positions; however, candidates who are independently eligible for employment authorization, including eligible F-1 students who obtain appropriate CPT or OPT authorization, may be considered.

Any required employment authorization must be in place before employment begins. If an intern is later considered for a full-time position, any need for future immigration sponsorship will be evaluated separately under Illumio’s immigration policy and the requirements of the position.

 

Our Commitment



Illumio believes that an environment of unique backgrounds, experiences, viewpoints, and individual contributions creates a culture of belonging, drives our future, and makes us stronger together in support of our customers and their success.



All official job offers from our company are extended directly by our recruitment team and will be sent through an official E-Signature document for your review and signature. Please be aware that we do not ask for any personal information in the process of extending offers of employment, such as financial details or social security numbers. Upon acceptance of any offer, we will request such information as part of the onboarding process prior to or on your first day of employment, and only after completing a background check through an authorized third-party vendor. If you receive any communication asking for personal details outside of these processes, please contact us immediately to verify the authenticity of the request. Your security is important to us, and we are committed to a safe and transparent hiring experience.

For roles in San Francisco and Los Angeles: Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring, Illumio will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

jobs.title: Partner Director, GTM Cloud Partnerships
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s GTM Partnerships team builds a strategic, global partner ecosystem that accelerates customer success, enables enterprise AI adoption, and drives durable growth in support of OpenAI’s mission.

Cloud partners are central to how customers discover, purchase, deploy, and scale OpenAI solutions. We work across cloud providers and their field, product, marketplace, technical, and partner organizations to reduce friction for customers and create repeatable paths from initial interest to production impact.

The team collaborates closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering, Finance, Legal, Security, Marketing, Operations, and Customer Success to turn strategic cloud relationships into measurable customer and commercial outcomes.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are hiring a Partner Director, GTM Cloud Partnerships to shape and execute OpenAI’s go-to-market strategy with strategic cloud partners.

You will own senior relationships across a portfolio of cloud providers and develop joint business plans that expand customer access to OpenAI’s products, generate partner-sourced opportunities, and accelerate enterprise adoption. You will translate company-level partnerships into practical field motions spanning account planning, co-selling, cloud marketplaces, customer procurement, technical enablement, solution development, and executive engagement.

This is a highly strategic and hands-on role. Success requires executive presence, strong commercial judgment, cloud ecosystem expertise, and the operating discipline to coordinate complex initiatives across multiple partners, regions, and internal teams. The ideal candidate can move fluidly between long-term strategy and the detailed execution required to deliver measurable results.

This role is based in San Francisco, Seattle, or New York. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Own the commercial engagement with a top global cloud partner in specific industry and customer segments, establishing strong alignment with their executive, sales, product, marketplace, technical, and partner organizations.

 - Build and run the partnership governance model for assigned customer segments, including pipeline reviews, forecasting, executive business reviews, milestone tracking, performance reporting, and escalation management.

 - Establish operating cadences for priority partnerships, including executive business reviews, pipeline inspections, forecasting, milestone tracking, performance reporting, and escalation management.

 - Identify, qualify, and accelerate partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities, working with OpenAI sellers to progress shared pursuits toward customer wins.

 - Develop and drive joint sales plays with cloud provider field teams and OpenAI Sales, including account mapping, joint account planning, opportunity identification, executive engagement, and deal progression.

 - Partner with Sales and Technical Success to identify, shape, and accelerate strategic enterprise opportunities involving cloud infrastructure, marketplaces, and AI transformation initiatives.

 - Collaborate with Partner Marketing on launches, campaigns, customer stories, field communications, and market-facing events.

 - Drive partner enablement across OpenAI products, use cases, technical capabilities, customer qualification, security, provisioning, and deployment best practices.

 - Represent OpenAI in executive meetings, customer engagements, strategic planning sessions, and industry events, requiring regular travel in North America. 

 - Gather structured feedback from cloud partners and customers and translate it into recommendations for OpenAI’s product, commercial, and go-to-market teams.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE

 - 10+ years of experience in cloud partnerships, strategic alliances, ecosystem sales, business development, or enterprise sales within cloud, SaaS, AI, or platform businesses.

 - Significant experience developing go-to-market partnerships with major cloud providers and navigating their sales, product, marketplace, technical, and partner organizations.

 - A demonstrated track record of producing measurable pipeline, revenue, customer adoption, or marketplace outcomes through strategic partnerships.

 - Strong familiarity with cloud marketplaces, co-sell programs, committed-spend models, partner attribution, and cloud-based enterprise procurement.

 - Experience supporting complex enterprise opportunities involving AI transformation, cloud modernization, data platforms, or large-scale technical deployments.

 - The ability to build trusted relationships with senior executives while remaining close to the operational details that determine whether a partnership succeeds.

 - Technical fluency sufficient to engage credibly with cloud architects, product leaders, engineering teams, and technical decision-makers.

 - The ability to influence without formal authority, manage escalations constructively, and create urgency across internal and external teams.

 - Experience operating in an early-stage or high-growth environment where strategies, processes, and playbooks are still being built.

 - Excellent written, verbal, negotiation, and executive-presentation skills.


YOU’LL BE ESPECIALLY SUCCESSFUL IF YOU

 - Can create structure in an ambiguous and rapidly evolving partnership landscape.

 - Combine a strategic perspective with a strong bias toward execution and measurable business outcomes.

 - Understand how cloud providers operate, from corporate strategy and product partnerships to marketplaces and field-level co-selling.

 - Build trust quickly with partners, customers, and internal stakeholders.

 - Learn technical concepts quickly and translate them into clear customer and commercial value.

 - Are energized by the opportunity to define how OpenAI works with the global cloud ecosystem to bring advanced AI into production for more organizations.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. 

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf.

In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

jobs.title: Sr. Remarketing Advisor, Pre-Owned - Atlanta
jobs.description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary As Sr. Remarketing Advisor, Pre‑Owned at Rivian, you will be responsible for managing acquired Rivian‑branded inventory through reconditioning processes at both internal service locations and with third‑party partners. Your role will be crucial in ensuring that vehicle quality meets Rivian’s high standards, optimizing internal and partner efficiency, and achieving internal goals and KPIs related to reconditioning quality, cycle time, cost, and inventory availability. You will work closely with cross‑functional teams to coordinate inbound and outbound logistics, streamline operations, and drive improvements in inventory management, reconditioning workflows, and overall vehicle quality. The ideal candidate has hands‑on experience in vehicle reconditioning or fixed operations, is comfortable with a fast‑paced, highly cross‑functional environment, and has an expertise and passion for electric vehicles. Responsibilities Oversee the end‑to‑end process of vehicle reconditioning from acquisition through final quality assurance and “front‑line ready” status, ensuring consistent standards across all locations. Coordinate inbound and outbound logistics for pre‑owned vehicles, including transportation scheduling, carrier and yard communication, gate‑in/gate‑out processes, and aligning vehicle movements with reconditioning and sales priorities. Coordinate with internal service locations and third‑party partners to ensure efficient and effective reconditioning operations, including scheduling, capacity management, and resolving blockers. Monitor and enforce quality standards throughout the reconditioning process, ensuring vehicles meet Rivian’s criteria for cosmetic, mechanical, software, and safety readiness. Own follow‑up with reconditioning vendors on quality issues, driving clear corrective actions, timelines, and verification steps to ensure vehicles consistently meet Rivian’s standards. Conduct regular audits and inspections at internal and partner locations to verify adherence to Rivian’s reconditioning and quality standards, and to identify gaps or training needs. Implement corrective actions and process improvements as needed to address quality, safety, or operational issues; document and standardize best practices across locations and partners. Develop, document, and continuously improve reconditioning workflows, including inspection processes, repair decision paths, parts ordering, detailing, software updates, and photo‑ready standards. Develop and maintain strong relationships with third‑party reconditioning partners (both existing and new), acting as the primary operational point of contact where appropriate. Evaluate partner performance based on efficiency, quality, throughput, logistics performance, and adherence to contractual and operational agreements; drive accountability and continuous improvement. Ensure adherence to internal goals, KPIs, and compliance requirements, including safety, regulatory, and internal policy standards. Work closely with internal teams such as Used Sales, Logistics, Service, Delivery, and Collision to ensure seamless operations across the vehicle life cycle. Provide regular updates and reports on inventory status, reconditioning progress, logistics performance, and partner performance to stakeholders and leadership. Train and mentor team members and partner teams on best practices, standard operating procedures, and Rivian quality expectations; support enablement as processes, tools, and policies evolve. Foster a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence, encouraging feedback, raising issues quickly, and partnering across teams to implement sustainable solutions. Qualifications Minimum of 3 years of experience in Vehicle reconditioning operations (or equivalent) experience. Significant hands‑on exposure to reconditioning processes preferred. inventory management, operations, or a related role within the automotive industry at either an Automotive OEM or a major used vehicle retailer. Strong understanding of vehicle reconditioning processes and quality standards, including experience with used‑car recon, service drive, body/cosmetic repair, or PDI workflows. Proven experience managing third‑party vendors or partners and maintaining strong, performance‑oriented relationships. Knowledge of automotive and EV service concepts and parts catalogs (e.g., ability to interpret repair orders, part numbers, and service operations). Excellent analytical skills with the ability to interpret operational and inventory data, identify trends, and make informed decisions and recommendations. Experience with business tools and software, including Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint; experience using data/BI tools (e.g., Tableau or similar) to track KPIs and performance is a plus. Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence cross‑functionally across Used Sales, Service, and Logistics, without direct authority. Experience working with and strong knowledge of electric vehicles and EV‑specific systems (battery, software, charging, etc.) is strongly preferred. Project management experience (formal or informal) is a plus, particularly in process improvement, partner onboarding, or multi‑site operational initiatives. Ability to work in a fast‑paced environment and manage multiple priorities, locations, and stakeholders simultaneously. Ability to work a flexible schedule to support operations on nights, weekends, and/or holidays as business needs require; willingness to travel (up to ~25%) to support reconditioning sites, partners, and launches. Physical Requirements Willingness to work in various working conditions, including full‑service retail or service centers, third‑party auction or reconditioning facilities, and outdoor environments with unpredictable weather. Physical exertion may be required to perform occupational tasks (sitting up to 2 or more hours at a time, standing for up to 8 or more hours a day, walking, bending, kneeling, laying, twisting, carrying, reaching, stretching, pushing, pulling, and lifting up to 50 lbs). Frequent use of hands for grasping and using tools correctly, entering data, writing communications, handling keys and vehicle components, or calling customers or internal partners. Strong understanding of written and spoken English. Ability to see, read, and interpret documents such as governmental regulations, safety rules, repair orders, inspection sheets, operating and maintenance instructions, or schematics. Pay Disclosure The salary range for this role is $71,900 to $90,100 for Georgia based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs. The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards. We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic partner, and children up to age 26, including but not limited to paid vacation, paid sick leave, and a competitive portfolio of insurance benefits including life, medical, dental, vision, short-term disability insurance, and long-term disability insurance to eligible employees. You may also have the opportunity to participate in Rivian’s 401(k) Plan and Employee Stock Purchase Program if you meet certain eligibility requirements. Full-time employee coverage is effective on their first day of employment. Part-time employee coverage is effective the first of the month following 90 days of employment. More information about benefits is available at rivianbenefits.com. You can apply for this role through careers.rivian.com (or through internal-careers-rivian.icims.com if you are a current employee). This job is not expected to be closed any sooner than 12-11-26. jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Ambient Product
jobs.description:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.



Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

About the Role:

Cohere seeks a strategic and detail-oriented Financial Analyst to join the budget planning, forecasting, and spend management team that covers multiple high-impact areas. This role will serve as a key finance partner to business units, providing actionable insights to drive smarter decisions and optimal financial controls. The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced environment, can juggle complex budget categories, and is comfortable challenging assumptions to ensure fiscal discipline.

You will own the preparation and management of the G&A budget and forecast across Finance, Legal, People, and Corporate Affairs, monitoring headcount, vendor, and operating expenses against plan. Working closely with department leaders, you will identify variances, provide insights into key cost drivers, and support disciplined resource allocation as the company scales. Beyond supporting the G&A function, you will also play a key role in driving organization-wide workforce planning.



As our Financial Analyst, you will manage:

 - Financial planning: Support roll-up of annual planning company-wide, corporate calendaring, and consolidated P&L

 - Budgeting & Forecasting: Build and maintain department-level budgets and company-wide forecasts, working closely with business leaders to align financial plans with operational goals.

 - Financial Modeling: Develop dynamic financial models to evaluate business scenarios, investment opportunities, and operational changes.

 - Reporting & Variance Analysis: Prepare monthly reporting packages, analyze variances between actuals, forecasts, and budgets, and communicate clear explanations to department leaders

 - Business Partnering: Serve as the finance point of contact for G&A budget owners, challenging assumptions and identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and cost discipline.

 - Data & Systems Management: Leverage financial systems (e.g., NetSuite, Google Sheets/Excel, Pigment) to ensure data accuracy, streamline processes, and improve reporting efficiency.

 - Workforce Planning: Support organization-wide workforce planning by developing and maintaining the workforce model, and establishing and refining key headcount and compensation assumptions.



This career opportunity may be a good match for you if you have:

 - Strong leadership, interpersonal, and communication skills, including effective communication skills at all levels within the Company and the ability to collaborate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Core Connectivity
jobs.description:
Zoox is building the world's most advanced self-driving hardware and software solution, and nearly every part of it depends on moving data reliably. Sensor frames to perception, planner decisions to vehicle controls, telemetry to the cloud, and remote operator video back down again. All of it crosses process, host, and network boundaries under hard latency and reliability budgets, on a vehicle that has to keep working when a link degrades or a network gets congested.
The Software Core Connectivity team owns that data path end to end: in-vehicle messaging (pub/sub, RPC, inter-process and inter-host transport), the vehicle's internal network, and vehicle-to-cloud connectivity. It also owns the transport and serialization abstractions the rest of the software organization builds on. Every one of those paths crosses a team boundary, so the work happens alongside firmware, product security, simulation, manufacturing, and IT, and those partners rely on this team for transport and networking depth to achieve their goals. As the team leader you will own the roadmap and the release commitments, and you will spend a real share of your time in those partnerships.

jobs.title: Revenue Accounting Manager
jobs.description:
ONWARDS TOGETHER!

Illumio is the leader in ransomware and breach containment, redefining how organizations contain cyberattacks and enable operational resilience. Powered by the Illumio AI Security Graph, our breach containment platform identifies and contains threats across hybrid multi-cloud environments – stopping the spread of attacks before they become disasters.

Recognized as a Leader in the Forrester Wave™ for Microsegmentation, Illumio enables Zero Trust, strengthening cyber resilience for the infrastructure, systems, and organizations that keep the world running.


LOCATION: 4 ON-SITE DAYS A WEEK IN SUNNYVALE, CA.




OUR TEAM’S VISION:

Our Finance team operates at the forefront of Zero Trust Segmentation, driving efficient growth and building strategic partnerships with key stakeholders. We focus on scalable infrastructure and an optimized financial model to support Illumio’s ambitious business goals.

 

As Illumio enters an exciting phase of growth, we’re looking for people who embody our values, deliver excellence, and drive innovation. Join us in shaping the future of cybersecurity while growing your career, where every contribution supports our collective success.



As the Technical Revenue Accounting Manager, you will help own and scale Illumio’s end-to-end revenue accounting lifecycle—from contract review and deal execution through revenue recognition, commissions, close, reporting, controls, and audit.

 

You’ll combine strong technical revenue accounting expertise with an operational mindset, partnering with Sales, Deal Desk, Legal, Finance, and other cross-functional teams to ensure transactions are accounted for accurately and supported by scalable processes.




YOUR IMPACT:

 - Manage key aspects of the end-to-end revenue accounting lifecycle, including contract review, revenue recognition, commissions accounting, month-end close, reconciliations, reporting, controls, and audit support.

 - Partner with Sales, Deal Desk, and Legal to review special-term quotes and provide accounting and operational guidance throughout the deal lifecycle.

 - Oversee day-to-day revenue accounting operations.

 - Manage sales commission accounting, reconciliations, and related financial reporting.

 - Develop and maintain revenue accounting policies, procedures, and desktop documentation.

 - Prepare ad hoc data and analysis for cross-functional partners.

 - Execute and enhance SOX controls, proactively identifying opportunities to strengthen the control environment.

 - Drive system automation and support system changes and validation to ensure smooth implementation of new initiatives.

 - Identify and implement AI and automation opportunities while continuously improving revenue accounting processes and procedures.


YOUR TOOLKIT:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA preferred.

 - 5+ years of progressive accounting experience, including revenue accounting in a SaaS, software, or technology company.

 - Strong knowledge of ASC 606 for complex, non-standard deals, with a solid understanding of revenue operations and the quote-to-cash process.

 - Strong analytical and advanced Excel skills, including experience working with large datasets and translating analysis into actionable business insights.

 - Hands-on experience with ERP and revenue recognition systems.

 - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment while balancing recurring operational responsibilities and strategic projects.

 - Salesforce experience is a plus.

 - Experience with sales commissions and contract acquisition costs under ASC 340-40 preferred.

 - Big Four public accounting experience preferred.

 #LI-OM1 #LI-ONSITE

 

Our Commitment



Illumio believes that an environment of unique backgrounds, experiences, viewpoints, and individual contributions creates a culture of belonging, drives our future, and makes us stronger together in support of our customers and their success.



All official job offers from our company are extended directly by our recruitment team and will be sent through an official E-Signature document for your review and signature. If you receive any communication asking for personal details outside of these processes, please contact us immediately to verify the authenticity of the request. Your security is important to us, and we are committed to a safe and transparent hiring experience.

jobs.title: Lifecycle Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
WHY SOCURE?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.




JOB OVERVIEW

Socure is hiring a Lifecycle Marketing Manager to own how prospects and customers move from first signal to pipeline. You will run lifecycle strategy across email and webinars, and you will build the signal-driven, agent-powered programs that decide who hears from us, when, and with what message.

This is an individual contributor role for a builder. You will define the signals that predict buying intent, then build AI agents and automated workflows that act on them in market: researching the account, writing the personalized message, sending it through the right channel, and handing warm accounts to Sales with context attached. Our marketing stack is changing, so we care more about how you think and build than about expertise in any single platform.

You will work closely with our AI-native Sales Development team, Digital Marketing, Field Marketing, Product Marketing, and Marketing Operations. Success is measured in qualified pipeline and revenue. Marketing Operations owns the platforms, data, scoring, routing, and attribution. You own the programs that run on top of them: who we talk to, what we say, and when.

 
 


JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own lifecycle strategy end to end
   
   - Set the lifecycle strategy and roadmap from first engagement through opportunity, expansion, and closed-lost re-engagement, tied to Socure’s funnel definitions and revenue targets.
   
   - Decide which programs we run, which we retire, and where AI and automation replace manual work.

 - Build signal-based programs
   
   - Define and rank the first- and third-party signals that predict buying intent, including web and content engagement, webinar behavior, intent data, hiring and funding changes, and opportunity stage movement in Salesforce.
   
   - Turn those signals into triggers with clear entry and exit rules, so each account gets a message that matches what it just did and Sales knows what was sent.

 - Design and deploy AI agents that run lifecycle programs in market
   
   - Build agents that act on signals externally: research the account and contact, draft personalized email and LinkedIn copy, choose timing and channel, and route high-intent accounts to Sales Development with context attached.
   
   - Set the guardrails for every agent, including brand voice, compliance review, human approval where the stakes call for it, and monitoring so performance improves over time.
   
   - Prototype fast with tools like Claude, Clay, Zapier or n8n, APIs, and our marketing automation platform, then turn what works into durable programs.

 - Own email as a channel
   
   - Run all lifecycle email, including signal-triggered sends, nurture, re-engagement, customer and expansion programs, and launch announcements.
   
   - Use AI to scale personalization by persona, industry, and account context while keeping a high bar for copy, design, and deliverability.

 - Turn webinars into pipeline
   
   - Own the webinar program on Zoom Webinars and ON24, from topic selection and speaker prep through promotion, live production, and follow-up.
   
   - Treat every webinar as a signal source: use registration, attendance, questions, and poll answers to trigger personalized follow-up and Sales handoffs within hours of the event.
   
   - Use AI to repurpose each webinar into recap emails, short clips, social posts, and sales assets.

 - Partner with Sales and Marketing Operations
   
   - Work with Sales Development on what a ready account looks like and the context each rep receives at handoff.
   
   - Give Marketing Operations the lifecycle requirements for the platform migration, scoring, and routing, and let them own the build.

 - Measure and experiment
   
   - Own the results of every lifecycle program, measured by signal-to-meeting conversion, signal-to-SQL rate, sourced and influenced pipeline, and velocity, using the reporting Marketing Operations maintains.
   
   - Run a steady testing cadence across signals, agent prompts, messaging, offers, timing, and webinar formats, and roll winners into standard programs.
   
   - Give marketing and sales leadership a clear, recurring readout on what is working, what is not, and what you are changing.

 - Protect trust and compliance
   
   - Make sure every program, whether run by a person or an agent, meets CAN-SPAM, GDPR, and CASL requirements, and flag data or deliverability issues to Marketing Operations.
   
   - Work with Legal and Compliance on standards for AI-generated outreach. Our buyers are fraud, risk, and compliance leaders in regulated industries, and every message reflects on Socure.

 - Demonstrate Socure leadership competencies
   
   - Operate with a strong test-and-learn mindset, bias for action, and ownership of outcomes.
   
   - Collaborate as “One Team” with cross-functional partners, communicate clearly, and use data to drive decisions and recommendations.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - 3-5+ years in B2B lifecycle, demand generation, or growth marketing at a high-growth technology company, with a track record of growing pipeline from mid-funnel programs.

 - Hands-on experience building signal-based or trigger-based programs that connect intent and engagement data to outreach and sales handoff.

 - Proof that you have built and shipped AI workflows or agents that run real marketing work. Bring examples to the interview.

 - Working knowledge of at least one modern marketing automation platform (Marketo, HubSpot, Customer.io http://Customer.io, or similar) and Salesforce. How fast you learn a new tool matters more than deep expertise in any one.

 - Experience running a webinar program that produced measurable pipeline.

 - Strong writing and editing skills, with good judgment about where AI output needs a human pass.

 - Comfort with data. You can build your own reports, and SQL or Python is a plus.

 - Nice to have: experience marketing to fraud, risk, identity, or compliance buyers in financial services or other regulated industries.

jobs.title: Novel Abuse Red Teamer
jobs.description:
About the Team

The Intelligence and Investigations team is dedicated to ensuring the safe, responsible deployment of AI by rapidly detecting and mitigating abuse. Our team leverages cutting-edge testing methodologies to uncover vulnerabilities and emerging threats, helping safeguard OpenAI’s products and users. We work closely with cross-functional partners across product, policy, and engineering to drive a comprehensive defense strategy against evolving adversarial challenges.

About the Role

As a Novel Abuse Red Teamer, you’ll advance our pre- and post-deployment testing efforts at OpenAI, ensuring our models and products remain resilient against evolving, real-world adversarial threats.

We are seeking a self-starter to design, execute, and refine innovative adversarial testing and simulation protocols that leverage state-of-the-art tools and a hands-on red team approach. In this role, you will simulate threat actor methodologies and conduct rigorous application testing to uncover novel abuse vectors.

You will serve as a critical technical bridge between our security, product, and policy teams by employing an attacker mindset and advanced red team tactics to drive actionable insights that strengthen our detection mechanisms and overall product defenses. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in application security or penetration testing, with hands-on experience in web application security and proficiency in tools such as Burp Suite, Metasploit, and similar. 
We value professionals with excellent communication skills, a commitment to continuous learning, and a passion for securing AI technologies through innovative testing methodologies.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and execute high-fidelity, realistic attack simulations that emulate sophisticated threat actor methodologies, uncovering hidden exploitation vectors through advanced red teaming and application testing techniques.

 - Analyze testing outcomes and generate actionable insights to refine our detection mechanisms, ultimately bolstering our overall security posture.

 - Serve as a crucial technical bridge between our security, product, and policy teams, ensuring that insights from adversarial testing inform broader defense strategies and remediation efforts.

 - Develop and integrate automation tools to streamline testing workflows and enable rapid iteration in response to emerging threats.

 - Collaborate closely with internal stakeholders to align testing strategies with evolving product needs and security objectives.

You might thrive in this role if you have / are:

 - Experience in application security, penetration testing, or red team operations, with a proven track record of executing adversarial testing and simulation protocols.

 - A strong technical background in web application security, coupled with hands-on expertise performing security testing of web applications, AI systems, and highly unique attack surfaces.

 - An attacker mindset and a passion for identifying novel abuse vectors in live environments, along with the ability to translate complex technical findings into actionable insights.

 - Demonstrated success in working cross-functionally within fast-paced, dynamic environments, managing complex product ecosystems, and driving rapid security enhancements.

 - Committed to continuous learning, innovation, and the pursuit of cutting-edge security methodologies to protect and advance AI technologies.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

jobs.title: Delivery Manager, Capacity Programs
jobs.description:
ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.




THE ROLE

We're looking for a Delivery Director,  Capacity Programs for our on-premises data center builds and neo cloud (GPU cloud) delivery programs. This is a high-visibility, execution-critical role sitting at the intersection of infrastructure engineering, capacity planning, vendor/partner management, and customer delivery.

You will own the end-to-end delivery lifecycle for large-scale compute infrastructure — from initial site/capacity commitments through power, networking, and hardware bring-up, to production-ready GPU/compute capacity landing in the hands of internal teams or customers. You'll be the person who turns ambitious infrastructure roadmaps into predictable, on-time,   delivery.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own delivery of on-prem infrastructure builds — colocation expansions, power/cooling readiness, rack-and-stack, network fabric bring-up, and hardware acceptance testing — coordinating across colo providers and partners, network engineering, hardware ops, and vendor teams.

 - Drive neo cloud delivery programs — manage capacity delivery from GPU cloud and neo cloud partners (e.g., colocation/bare-metal/GPU cloud providers), including contract milestones, capacity ramps, SLAs, and go-live readiness.

 - Build and maintain master delivery schedules across concurrent, multi-site, multi-vendor programs, integrating power/shell timelines, hardware lead times, logistics, and software/platform readiness into a single critical path.

 - Manage cross-functional stakeholders — engineering, data center operations, procurement, finance, legal, and executive leadership — translating technical dependencies into clear program status, risks, and decisions.

 - Own vendor and partner relationships for infrastructure delivery, including neo cloud providers, colocation partners, hardware OEMs, and logistics/installation contractors; hold partners accountable to contractual delivery commitments.

 - Run risk and dependency management — identify critical path risks (power availability, hardware lead times, permitting, supply chain), drive mitigation, and escalate proactively rather than reactively.

 - Establish delivery governance — standardized program frameworks, milestone definitions, RAID logs, capacity tracking, and reporting cadences (weekly ops reviews, executive/board-level updates).

 - Drive capacity planning alignment — partner with demand/capacity planning teams to ensure delivery timelines match business commitments (customer contracts, internal growth targets).

 - Lead post-mortems and continuous improvement — after major builds or delivery milestones, drive retrospectives that improve cost, speed, and predictability of future builds.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required:

 - 8+ years in technical program management, delivery management, or infrastructure program leadership, with at least 3+ years managing large-scale physical infrastructure or data center delivery programs.

 - Demonstrated experience delivering on-prem data center builds (power, cooling, network, rack-and-stack) from planning through go-live.

 - Direct experience with GPU cloud / neo cloud capacity delivery: understanding of GPU cluster architectures (e.g., InfiniBand/RoCE fabrics, rack power density, liquid cooling considerations) and the commercial/operational mechanics of capacity contracts with neo cloud or colocation providers.

 - Track record managing complex, multi-vendor, multi-workstream programs with hard external deadlines and significant financial/business exposure.

 - Strong executive communication skills. Able to distill complex technical/operational risk into clear, decision-ready updates for senior leadership.

 - Proven vendor/partner management experience, including negotiating delivery commitments and holding partners accountable.

 - Comfortable operating with ambiguity in a fast-moving, high-growth environment. Bias toward action and structured problem-solving.

Preferred:

 - Experience at a hyperscaler, neo cloud provider, colocation company, or AI infrastructure company

 - Familiarity with GPU hardware lifecycles (NVIDIA H100/H200/GB200 class systems), power/thermal constraints, and supply chain dynamics for compute.

 - PMP, PgMP, or equivalent program management certification.

 - Experience building delivery/program management functions from the ground up



BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

 - (U.S. only) 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents

 - Flexible PTO policy including company wide Winter Break (our offices are closed from Christmas Eve to New Year's Day!)

 - Paid parental leave

 - Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

 - (U.S. only) Company-facilitated 401(k)

 - Exposure to a variety of ML startups, offering unparalleled learning and networking opportunities.

Apply now to embark on a rewarding journey in shaping the future of AI! If you are a motivated individual with a passion for machine learning and a desire to be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking team, we would love to hear from you.

At Baseten, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, genetic information, disability, or veteran status.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable law (by example, the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, where applicable).

jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE 

We are looking for a Legal & Privacy Operations Associate to help the Ramp legal team scale with product and operational leverage as the business grows. You will keep legal requests moving, administer core tools and records, and automate corporate, policy, and privacy program work with Legal and cross-functional partners to accelerate Ramp’s AI products and growth.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Workplace Planning & Programming
jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

Crusoe is looking for a Senior Manager, Workplace Planning & Programming to help shape how we plan, optimize, and scale our corporate workplaces as the business continues to grow. This role will be responsible for translating business needs, headcount forecasts, and workplace utilization into actionable space plans, workplace programs, and recommendations that support both current and future business needs. This includes helping set the program standards for workplace services, including F&B and amenities, that shape how employees experience our offices.

You'll work closely with business leaders, Finance, People, Real Estate, and Workplace teams to understand how our teams work today and anticipate what they'll need in the future. You'll partner with the Senior Portfolio Director on site selection and real estate evaluations, bringing workplace planning expertise into decisions about new offices, relocations, and expansions. You'll also play an active role in corporate office projects already underway, stepping in to assess space requirements, evaluate planning options, and drive cross-functional alignment on workplace requirements at various stages of the project lifecycle.

This is a people management role that blends strategic leadership and planning with hands-on execution and team development. You'll lead complex workplace planning initiatives, develop recommendations for senior leadership, and establish scalable processes that bring greater consistency, rigor, and accountability to how Crusoe plans its workplaces. You'll need to be comfortable navigating ambiguity, jumping into projects already in motion, and driving workplace planning workstreams forward in a fast-paced, evolving environment. You’ll propose and lead workplace strategy recommendations for the Head of Workplace, who sets the strategy. You’ll drive workplace planning and programming work, with the Head of Workplace as approver, and partner with Workplace Operations and site teams to roll out program standards.



What You'll Be Working On:

 - Workplace Planning & Capacity Management
   
   - Lead corporate workplace capacity planning and space requirements analysis, translating business growth, headcount forecasts, and organizational needs into actionable workplace plans.
   
   - Partner with Finance, People, and business leaders to evaluate hiring plans, team adjacencies, attendance patterns, and future space requirements.
   
   - Develop capacity models and planning scenarios to identify opportunities for expansion, consolidation, densification, and optimization of existing corporate spaces.
   
   - Analyze workplace utilization and employee work patterns to inform planning recommendations and improve space efficiency.
   
   - Partner with the Senior Portfolio Director to evaluate how workplace capacity needs and planning scenarios inform broader real estate portfolio decisions.
   
   - Support active corporate office projects by assessing existing plans, identifying requirements gaps, and driving workplace planning workstreams forward alongside project owners.
   
   - Present data-driven workplace planning recommendations to leadership, balancing employee experience, operational needs, cost considerations, and future flexibility.
   
   - Bring together employee feedback and survey data, workplace utilization and occupancy data, and on-the-ground insights from site workplace teams to propose and lead workplace strategy recommendations and input into the multi-year roadmap.

 - Site Selection & Real Estate Evaluation
   
   - Partner with the Senior Portfolio Director to support site selection for new corporate offices, relocations, and expansions, bringing workplace requirements and functional planning expertise into the process.
   
   - Work closely with real estate brokers and internal stakeholders on market evaluations, property tours, site comparisons, and recommendations.
   
   - Develop workplace-specific site evaluation criteria that consider capacity, location, accessibility, team adjacencies, functionality, employee experience, and future growth.
   
   - Evaluate potential properties and space configurations to identify functional constraints, opportunities, and planning trade-offs.
   
   - Collaborate with Finance and the Senior Portfolio Director on site comparisons and business case development, providing capacity scenarios, workplace planning assumptions, and functional requirements.
   
   - Support leadership recommendations and the transition into lease negotiations, ensuring workplace requirements remain reflected in transaction decisions.

 - Business Case Development & Financial Partnership
   
   - Partner with Finance, Real Estate, and Project Management to develop business cases, evaluate planning scenarios, and assess trade-offs across capacity, cost, functionality, and employee experience.
   
   - Own workplace planning assumptions, capacity scenarios, and functional requirements that inform financial evaluations.
   
   - Develop clear, data-driven recommendations that support leadership decisions on workplace investments and space requirements.
   
   - Present findings and recommendations to senior stakeholders to support timely and informed decision-making.
   
   - Partner with the Real Estate & Workplace Project Manager to ensure planning recommendations align with project budgets and delivery considerations, while the Project Manager retains ownership of project budgets.

 - Workplace Programming & Design Partnership
   
   - Own workplace programming and functional requirements for corporate office projects, ensuring spaces are designed to support how teams work and collaborate.
   
   - Translate headcount forecasts, team requirements, and workplace standards into detailed space programs that inform design.
   
   - Partner with architects, designers, and the Real Estate & Workplace Project Manager to ensure business requirements are reflected throughout the design process.
   
   - Review proposed layouts and design solutions for functionality, capacity, flexibility, and employee experience.
   
   - Identify and communicate risks or trade-offs when design decisions may impact approved business requirements, escalating conflicts with budget or schedule as needed.
   
   - Serve as the primary representative of business and employee needs throughout the design process, while the Real Estate & Workplace Project Manager retains accountability for design management, vendor selection, construction, project budgets, schedule, and delivery.

 - Workplace Service Programs.
   
   - Help set program standards for workplace services across sites, including F&B, amenities, front-of-house, etc. in partnership with the Head of Workplace and Workplace Operations.
   
   - Define service levels and standards by site type so offices of similar size get a consistent experience.
   
   - Define the space and infrastructure that service programs need (kitchens, pantries, mailrooms, storage, reception) during programming and build-out.

jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Corporate Security at Ramp owns the identity and access layer for the company: Okta, Google Workspace, the SaaS applications behind them, and the governance that decides who holds what. We are hiring a Senior Security Engineer, Identity, to turn that layer into IAM as a service — a platform the rest of Ramp can use without filing a ticket.

 

The role is hands-on. You will design how identity works at Ramp and write the code that implements it: identity configuration in Terraform, entitlements created and governed through an agentic workflow, and an on-call agent that answers access questions before anyone has to ask a person. As more access flows between applications and AI agents rather than people, you will own how those identities are issued, scoped, and audited.

 

You will report to the Corporate Security lead and work closely with IT, Security Engineering, AI DevX, and the Data team.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own Terraform for identity services: Okta applications, authorization servers, authentication policies, groups and group rules, and SCIM provisioning

 - Design and operate custom authorization servers, including audiences, scopes, claims, and access policies for internal services and AI agents

 - Implement app-to-app and agent access through Cross App Access (XAA) and ID-JAG, so delegated access is brokered and governed by the IdP rather than granted user by user

 - Own our IGA platform: the entitlement catalog, ownership, access requests, time-bound grants, and certifications

 - Build the agentic workflow that takes a team from "I have a new group of people who need access to X" to a defined, owned, and governed entitlement, with the Terraform and IGA changes opened for review

 - Build identity graphs with ISPM tooling to target overprivileged and long-standing access across human and non-human identities

 - Build the identity data lake behind an on-call agent that can explain events like a User Not Assigned Application error in Okta before the employee opens a ticket




WHAT YOU NEED

 - 6+ years in identity engineering or IAM, including operational ownership of Okta or an equivalent identity provider at scale

 - Deep understanding of OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, and SCIM, including how custom authorization servers issue and enforce aud, scope, and claims

 - Working knowledge of how XAA and ID-JAG work under the hood, including token exchange and JWT bearer grants

 - Experience with ISPM or identity graph tooling, and turning its findings into automated remediation

 - Experience owning an IGA platform or building the equivalent in-house

 - Terraform experience managing identity providers, including module design, state, and CI

 - Programming in Python or Go, with experience building against platform APIs




BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

 - Budget for intra-office travel

 - Weekly coffee stipend




UNITED STATES

jobs.title: Senior Manager, GTM & Revenue Finance
jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Senior Manager to lead GTM and Revenue Finance as part of the Strategic Finance team. This person will have direct exposure to the CFO, CRO and board materials. You will lead a team of analysts to forecasting, reporting and strategic initiatives for our GTM organization. You will have ownership of the revenue line and the chance to build the function, the team and the systems rather than inherit them. 




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES




REVENUE FORECASTING AND DEAL ECONOMICS

 - Own the ARR and revenue plan by segment, region, product and deployment type

 - Build driver-based models connecting sales pipeline to ARR and GAAP revenue conversion

 - Triangulate top-down targets against bottoms-up deal pipeline and deal-level economics

 - Run scenario planning and sensitivities to support a dynamic market landscape

 - Own gross margin annual planning and explain the storyline on variances and performance

 - Provide guidance on deal structuring, terms, margin profile, etc

 - Define and track KPIs including LTV, CAC, payback period, gross margin

 - Establish a mature framework for deal review and acceptance working closely with Rev Ops, Biz Ops and GTM




ROI ANALYSIS & STRATEGIC INITIATIVES

 - Analyze territory and segment economics including CAC efficiency and payback period

 - Partner with Marketing and Sales leadership to allocate spend toward the highest-return motions

 - Report GTM performance monthly finance and business reviews

 - Own the GTM financial narrative in board and executive packages

 - Run investor diligence, the data room and customer reference prep during fundraising

 - Build product finance capabilities as product mix expands, including product-line P&L, unit economics and gross margin by revenue stream




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 12+ years of progressive experience in Financial Planning & Analysis and Strategic Finance

 - Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; MBA or CFA preferred.

 - Strong proficiency in financial modeling, forecasting, and budgeting

 - Experience with EPM Systems (Anaplan, Pigment, Onestream) and BI tools (Tableau, Power BI, Looker)

 - Excellent analytical skills with ability to interpret complex financial data

 - Exceptional communication skills—the ability to tell a compelling story through data

 - Experience building and scaling FP&A functions in high-growth and ambiguous environments

 - Deep understanding of GAAP accounting and the interaction between the P&L, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow statement.
   


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience at fast-moving technology companies, particularly with GTM business partners

 - Startup experience, particularly in scaling financial operations

 - Familiarity with SaaS metrics and AI business models

 - Experience with fundraising, investor relations, and board reporting

 - Experience implementing financial systems and automation solutions




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.



We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.



Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

jobs.title: Executive in Residence, Cyber
jobs.description:
About the role

OpenAI is seeking an accomplished CISO/CSO or equivalent cybersecurity executive to help security leaders turn frontier AI into practical cyber defense. As an Executive in Residence, you will be a visible industry voice and a trusted peer to senior customer and partner leaders, working alongside our account, technical, product, research, and deployment teams.

We are looking for someone security leaders already want to hear from in person and digitally. You bring a recognized reputation, substantive operating experience, and a record of attracting senior audiences through the quality of your ideas and judgment. Your participation should make an industry agenda more compelling and bring the right leaders into the room.

You will combine invited speaking and executive engagement with the work needed to move customers from interest to adoption. You will also bring field insights into OpenAI’s cyber efforts and advance selected strategic initiatives agreed with cyber leadership.

About OpenAI Cyber

Cybersecurity is entering a period of fundamental disruption, and AI creates an opportunity to raise the bar for defense across the entire industry. At OpenAI, we are bringing together frontier research, security products, and partnerships to help defenders scale their expertise, protect more systems, and close the gap between identifying risk and taking action. Our ambition is to make stronger security achievable for organizations of every size and help the industry rethink what effective defense can look like. Joining now means helping shape that transformation while its foundations are still being built. For an experienced security leader, this is an opportunity to turn hard-earned judgment into capabilities that empower defenders worldwide—and influence the standards, practices, and technology that define the next era of cybersecurity.

In this role, you will:

 - Represent OpenAI in consequential industry conversations. Deliver invited keynotes, contribute to substantive panels, and lead executive briefings on AI and cyber defense. Develop original talks and articles grounded in operating experience, evidence, and practical lessons.

 - Convene senior security leaders. Use your reputation and relationships to attract relevant audiences and host candid CISO dinners, closed-door roundtables, and peer discussions. Build lasting relationships across your region or priority industries.

 - Help customers make decisions and deploy. Work with account and technical teams to identify priority defensive workflows, build executive sponsorship, address organizational barriers, and shape pilots with clear objectives, owners, and next steps toward deployment.

 - Bring the field into product and research. Capture customer needs, adoption barriers, and deployment lessons. Translate recurring themes into specific recommendations for product, research, and field teams, and help assess whether changes address the underlying problem.

 - Advance strategic initiatives. Lead selected projects where your executive experience, industry relationships, or ability to coordinate across teams can accelerate progress. Establish the intended outcome and follow through with the relevant owners.

 - Strengthen field effectiveness. Help teams prepare for senior security conversations, develop useful executive briefing materials, and turn engagements into sustained relationships and agreed actions.

 - You will prioritize independently invited thought leadership, major industry forums, and curated executive engagements consistent with the program’s speaking principles. Each engagement should have a clear purpose, an appropriate audience, and an owner for follow-through.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Experience as a CISO or equivalent security executive with direct accountability for a substantial security program, including difficult decisions about risk, investment, incidents, and organizational change.

 - An established reputation among senior security leaders in a relevant region, sector, or the broader industry. You can demonstrate that your participation attracts executive audiences and earns invitations to respected forums.

 - A strong speaking record and the ability to hold a room, handle unscripted questions, and lead candid peer discussions. Your communication is clear, technically credible, and useful to the audience.

 - Technical depth to discuss security architecture and defensive operations with practitioners, and the judgment to explain the capabilities, limitations, and implications of AI to executives and boards.

 - Trusted relationships with CISOs and other senior technology leaders, plus a record of building relationships beyond your existing network.

 - Experience turning executive alignment into action across teams, with evidence of adoption, deployment, or measurable improvements in security outcomes.

 - The ability to listen closely, exercise discretion, and represent customer needs accurately. You work effectively with commercial and technical colleagues and distinguish evidence from speculation.

Additional experience we value

 - Deep experience in technology, retail, telecommunications, life sciences, or healthcare, or a strong regional security leadership network.

 - Practical work applying AI to security, leading enterprise technology adoption, or advising organizations through significant changes in security operations.

 - Published practitioner work, influential research, or sustained contributions to security communities that demonstrate the substance behind your public reputation.

This role involves regular travel for customer meetings and industry engagements.

How success will be measured

 - Demand for your participation in respected industry forums, the relevance and seniority of audiences you attract, and the quality of the discussions you lead.

 - Scale and scope of your online presence sharing OpenAI’s message.

 - Stronger executive relationships that result in clear customer decisions, well-scoped pilots, and progress toward sustained deployment.

 - Specific field insights that influence product, research, or deployment decisions, and delivery of agreed strategic initiatives.

 - Practical content and briefings that customers and field teams use, with evidence that engagements lead to useful follow-through.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.
