jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Agentic Analytics
jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


WHY THIS ROLE?

We're building the foundational infrastructure that will define how the world thinks about and deploys AI, and we want the sharpest, most driven, and most curious people to help us do it. As the founding lead of Agentic Analytics, a new team in our Analytics and Data Insights organization, you'll own how Cohere gets answers from its own data: an agentic analytics system that answers business questions over governed data, shows the source, query, and freshness behind every answer, and asks for clarification or declines when the evidence is insufficient.

Agentic analytics is far from a solved problem, and correctness is the hard part. A query that runs can still answer the wrong question. Agents go wrong when a business term maps to more than one table, when data goes stale, and when the right context never reaches the model. The worst failures are silent and plausible: a join that double-counts, a wrong denominator, missing data read as zero. Getting this right takes governed definitions, context an agent can use, and an evaluation bar that decides what ships.

You'll build on work already in motion: an internal analytics agent in pilot on our BigQuery warehouse, which is fed by tested ingestion pipelines and modeled in dbt. In your first year, you'll take it to production for teams across Cohere, one domain at a time, and make it replicable: each new domain stands up with configuration, a fresh evaluation set, and very little new code.

This is a hands-on  staff engineering role reporting to our Senior Director of Data Analytics. You'll write production code and evaluation sets yourself while managing a small founding team that grows as the system proves itself. You may have held the title software engineer, AI engineer, or data scientist; what matters is that you've built a system like this and run it in production.



RESPONSIBILITIES

As the lead of Agentic Analytics, you will:

 - Own the system end to end. Set the architecture for how a business question becomes a governed query and a verifiable answer: interpreting the question, retrieving the right context, applying approved definitions and joins, enforcing the asking user's permissions, and attaching the evidence (source, query, freshness) to every answer.

 - Build and run it in production. Design the core services and write much of the first version yourself: agent-facing data tools (MCP or equivalent), context retrieval, agent skills for analytics, and the APIs that serve answers. Hold them to production standards for reliability, latency, cost, security, and observability. Put it where people already work: Slack, North, IDEs, and other agents.

 - Hold every release to the evaluation bar. Build and run the evaluation harness, and define what correct means in each domain: ground-truth question sets, including held-out cases and questions the agent should clarify or decline; result-level scoring, correct-or-decline rates, coverage, and error severity; and regression tests on every change to context, skills, or models. Nothing ships below the bar, and the call on when a domain is ready for production is yours.

 - Engineer the context layer. Turn metric definitions, approved joins, documentation generated from the code that builds each table, a business glossary, and worked examples into context the agent can use. Every correction becomes a reviewed definition and a regression test.

 - Roll it out across Cohere. Bring domains such as marketing, revenue, finance, and product onto the system one at a time, each with named owners, certified definitions, and its own evaluation set. Measure adoption, accuracy, turnaround, and correction effort against how those teams work today.

 - Make it replicable. Package the tools, skills, context templates, and evaluations, and document them well enough that other teams at Cohere can run the system without you.

 - Hire and lead the team. Bring on the team's first engineers, set the technical bar, review the work, and develop the people doing it.

 - Partner across Cohere. Work with our data platform team on the warehouse and semantic models, our model evaluation team on evaluation methodology, our security team on access, and each domain's owners on definitions and rollout.


QUALIFICATIONS

You may be a good fit, if you have:

 - 10+ years building and operating production analytics or software systems, including technical leadership of a team or of systems that span teams

 - Experience shipping LLM agents to production: tool use, MCP or similar, retrieval and context engineering, guardrails, and observability, with firm opinions on where they fail

 - Hands-on experience building natural-language or agentic analytics (text-to-SQL, analytics agents, question answering over a semantic layer) that real users relied on, and evidence that it was right

 - Depth in evaluating LLM systems: golden sets, result-level comparison, abstention metrics, error taxonomies, and regression testing in CI, plus the judgment to tell a good demo from a system you'd put in front of a CFO

 - Strong Python and SQL, and experience designing and running production services and APIs on a major cloud (Google Cloud is a plus)

 - Fluency with data: cloud warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar), dbt, and semantic layers (MetricFlow, LookML, Cube, or similar). You think in grain, metric definitions, and approved joins, and you can tell when a number is wrong before it reaches a decision

 - Experience building identity-aware access for agents, where the agent acts with the asking user's permissions and every query leaves an audit trail

 - Experience hiring and developing engineers, with a leadership style grounded in empathy as much as in data

 - Genuine excitement about AI: you follow the research, have opinions, and enjoy being in the weeds

 - Comfort operating in ambiguity, leading through partners you don't manage, and writing design docs and eval reports that settle decisions across teams

If some of the above doesn't line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply!




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.

All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Backend, Comms Platform
jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Every approval request, receipt reminder, payment alert, and card notification Ramp sends has to reach the right person, on the right channel, at the right time. When it does, finance teams close faster and employees spend less time chasing tasks. When it doesn't, a missed message can mean a stalled approval, a late payment, or a flood of notifications nobody asked for.



Ramp's Communications Platform team builds the shared system that every product team uses to reach customers. It handles transactional messages across email, SMS, push, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and WhatsApp, including templating, delivery, retries, digesting, user preferences, and delivery monitoring. The team also supports the conversational experiences that let customers work with Ramp directly from the channels they already use.



We're looking for a backend engineer to own a core part of that platform. You'll take responsibility for an area such as message delivery and channel integrations, communication preferences, or platform reliability and scale, set its technical direction within the team, and keep it correct and dependable as message volume and the number of teams building on it grow. You'll work closely with product, design, and engineering partners across Ramp to make communications faster, more reliable, and easier for every team to build on.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the design and evolution of a core part of Ramp's communications platform, from technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration

 - Build and extend integrations with messaging channels and delivery providers, including email, SMS, push, and workplace chat tools such as Slack and Microsoft Teams

 - Design delivery workflows that are idempotent, retry safely, and confirm successful delivery, so customers reliably get the messages they need without duplicate sends

 - Build communication preferences and controls that let users and administrators decide what they receive and where

 - Make the platform simple and safe for other Ramp engineers to build on, with clear abstractions, strong defaults, and good developer tooling

 - Improve the reliability, performance, and observability of the platform as message volume grows

 - Drive technical direction for your area and raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - Experience designing, building, and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows

 - A track record of owning a system or product area end to end and shaping its technical direction over time

 - Strong system design judgment, especially around reliability, idempotency, and correctness in high-volume distributed systems

 - Product sense: you care about the experience of the people receiving each message, not just the ticket, and you balance speed with quality

 - Clear communication and a collaborative approach to technical decisions across product, design, and engineering
   
   


NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience building notification, messaging, or communications platforms

 - Experience integrating with messaging providers or channel APIs, such as Twilio, SendGrid, Slack, Microsoft Teams, or WhatsApp

 - Experience building internal platforms or shared services used by many engineering teams

 - Experience scaling high-volume, event-driven, or queue-based systems




BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

 - Flexible PTO

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

 - Budget for intra-office travel

 - Weekly coffee stipend




UNITED STATES

OTHER NOTICES

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Financial Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.


About the role:

Make Replit the single place where businesses can buy everything they need through their agents. As a Staff Software Engineer on Replit’s Money team, you’ll set technical direction and build the commerce platform that lets users discover, evaluate, purchase, and manage the products and services they need to build and run their businesses—without leaving Replit.

 

Replit already enables businesses to accept payments through integrations such as Stripe. This role builds on that foundation to expand what businesses can buy and accomplish through Replit Agent. You’ll design commerce experiences that combine the simplicity consumers expect with the controls enterprises need, making agent-assisted purchasing useful, trustworthy, and reliable.

 

You’ll own architecture and lead cross-team delivery across merchant and service-provider integrations, agent tools, purchasing workflows, and the lifecycle after a transaction. The challenge goes beyond executing a payment: agents need to understand what a user wants, present clear choices and costs, act within delegated authority, and verify that the purchase delivered the intended outcome. You’ll stay hands-on with design and code while aligning partners, mentoring engineers, and turning an ambitious product vision into incremental customer value.


You will:

 - Set technical direction for Replit’s financial infrastructure, with an immediate focus on enterprise billing, spend controls, and financial correctness.

 - Build shared services for usage-based billing, pricing, credits, subscriptions, and entitlements so product teams can launch without rebuilding billing.

 - Automate enterprise contract lifecycles—from onboarding through amendments and renewals—keeping commercial terms, provisioned credits, and invoices in sync.

 - Build timely budget enforcement, alerts, and overrides that give customers control over spend without disrupting their hosted apps.

 - Make AI usage understandable: attribute costs to the right customer, workspace, user, or agent, including delegated work without double-counting.

 - Build reconciliation and audit trails that make balances and invoices explainable and help Finance catch discrepancies before customers do.

 - Simplify the billing stack through safe migrations that preserve balances, transaction history, and customer access.

 - Own production reliability through testing, observability, incident response, and safe recovery from duplicate events, delayed usage, and partial failures.

 - Stay hands-on while leading cross-team delivery, mentoring engineers, and partnering with Product, Finance, Sales, and Support.


Required skills and experience:

 - A track record of Staff-level technical ownership: setting architecture and delivering complex initiatives across teams.

 - Deep experience building and operating production backend or distributed systems.

 - Strong fundamentals in API design, data modeling, databases, and event-driven architecture.

 - Sound judgment around transactions, consistency, concurrency, idempotency, and failure recovery.

 - Experience evolving live systems and migrating data without compromising correctness or availability.

 - Product judgment that balances customer needs, delivery speed, and long-term system quality.

 - Clear communication with technical and non-technical partners, including translating business requirements into system behavior.

 - Hands-on leadership through implementation, design reviews, mentoring, and production ownership.


Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience with billing, payments, subscriptions, credits, entitlements, or other financial systems.

 - Experience with enterprise contracts, negotiated pricing, invoicing, or quote-to-cash automation.

 - Experience with high-volume usage metering, pricing calculations, or low-latency spend controls.

 - Experience building reconciliation, financial reporting, or auditable transaction histories with Finance and Accounting.

 - Experience integrating billing, payment, or CRM platforms, with judgment about what to build versus buy.

 

Bonus Points:

 - Experience with AI or cloud infrastructure billing, including variable costs and attribution across distributed workloads.

 - Experience building customer-facing spend visibility, budgets, or internal tools that reduce manual billing work.

 - Experience with cloud marketplace billing, payment recovery, or fraud and dispute workflows.

 - Familiarity with agentic commerce or delegated spending. These are additional strengths, not requirements.



What we value:

 - Customer outcomes: success means a business can get what it needs through its agent, with clear costs and a verified result—not merely a completed API call.

 - User control and trust: agents act within explicit authority, surface consequential choices, and make purchases and ongoing commitments understandable.

 - Consumer simplicity and enterprise readiness: straightforward experiences should coexist with the controls organizations need.

 - End-to-end ownership: we own the experience from intent through purchase, fulfillment, and ongoing management.

 - Pragmatic technical leadership: we build on what exists, deliver incremental value, and invest in correctness and extensibility where they matter.

 - Clear collaboration: we document decisions, surface risks early, and help other teams and partners succeed.



Full-Time Employee Benefits Include:

💰 Competitive Salary & Equity

💹 401(k) Program with a 4% match (US Only)

⚕️ Health, Dental, Vision and Life Insurance

🩼 Short Term and Long Term Disability

🚼 Paid Parental, Medical, Caregiver Leave

🏝 Flexible Time Off (FTO) + Holidays

🚗 Commuter Benefits  (In-Office & US Only)

📱 Monthly Wellness Stipend

🧑‍💻 Autonomous Work Environment

🖥 In Office Set-Up Reimbursement (In-Office Only)

🚀 Quarterly Team Gatherings

☕ In Office Amenities (In-Office Only)

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Access Management
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management. 

We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation, more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.

You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries. 

The Opportunity

Every day, a security administrator somewhere decides who can open which door. A new nurse starts on Monday and needs the medication room but not the server closet. A contractor needs the loading dock for three weeks. Someone leaves the company at 5pm and their badge should stop working at 5:01. Multiply that by 200,000 employees across 400 sites, and you have one of the largest and least-solved logistical problems in enterprise software.

Access control is Verkada's second largest business: hundreds of millions of dollars in sales, growing 40 to 60% year over year, with roughly 80 people building in this area. Access management is the pillar that decides whether all of that feels effortless or exhausting.

We are hiring a Lead Product Manager to own it end to end: users, identities, groups, policies, requests, access levels, and visitor access, from the moment an admin expresses intent to the moment a door opens for the right person.

We do this well today. We think it can be dramatically better, through interfaces that make scale feel simple, APIs and integrations that let the system run itself, and agents that let an admin state what they want instead of clicking through configuration. You will own that as a vertical slice: web and mobile, the backend behind them, the configuration we push to door hardware, and the API and agent surfaces we expose. You will work with a dedicated designer, an engineering manager, and a dedicated engineering team.

We are committed to a thriving in-office culture. This role requires you to work onsite at our HQ in San Mateo, CA.

The access model and administrator interfaces: get the core concepts right

  • Own users, groups, credentials, access levels, door associations, and schedules. This is the conceptual core of the product, and getting it right is the difference between an admin who trusts the system and one who works around it
  • Own the administrative interfaces and experience across web and mobile: bulk operations, search, and review flows that stay fast when a customer has 200,000 users and 10,000 doors
  • Own visitor access, including how guests are invited, credentialed, and expired

Provisioning and integrations: let the system run itself

  • Own the API and integration surface. Most large customers want access to follow their identity provider and HR system automatically, so joiners, movers, and leavers are handled without anyone touching our UI
  • Partner with Verkada's Core team to drive identity integration: SCIM provisioning, SSO, directory sync, and the mapping between an HR record and what a door actually does

Agents and natural language: let admins state intent

  • Define how agents fit into access management. An admin should be able to say what they want and have the system propose the configuration that satisfies it
  • Define the guardrails. Anything that changes who can open a physical door needs review, attribution, and a clean path to undo
  • Build the evaluation framework: accuracy, escalation rate, and how we know a proposed change is safe before it ships to a door

Security posture: surface what looks wrong before it becomes an incident

  • Build the proactive layer: over-provisioned users, credentials that outlived their purpose, access patterns that do not match a door's sensitivity
  • Own audit and compliance reporting, including what a customer hands an auditor to prove who had access to what, and when

Direction

  • Set the direction for access management over multiple years, not just the next few releases, and make the case for it to engineering leadership and the exec team
  • Become the person at Verkada who understands access administrators best. You will define the personas and jobs to be done for this area and make that framework something the rest of the org uses
  • Raise the bar for the product managers around you. You will work alongside four other PMs in access control, and we expect your standards for research, writing, and decision-making to show up in their work too

How You'll Work

  • Own customer discovery. Talk to security administrators directly, go on site walks, and watch someone badge through a building to see where the model breaks down in the real world
  • Set strategy and prioritize the roadmap, balancing reliability, new capability, and the loudest customer in the room
  • Prototype constantly. We expect you to build things to think, not only to write specs about them. You will do this in the interview process too
  • Partner closely with engineering and design, bringing both technical depth and design sense
  • Drive execution from spec to launch with obsessive attention to detail
  • Craft the product pitch with marketing and sales, and help the field sell a capability that is often the reason a deal closes
  • Stay on top of the competitive landscape, the identity ecosystem, and where the market is going
  • Hold several time horizons at once: learning from customers now, planning six and twelve months out, and shipping what launches next quarter

What you'll bring

  • 6+ years of product management experience, currently at Senior or Lead scope. You have owned a product area, not a single feature, and you set its direction rather than executing someone else's
  • Experience with B2B software used by administrators at scale. with a track record of building and scaling complex enterprise products. Permissions, identity, provisioning, policy, or configuration-heavy admin tooling is directly relevant, as is any product where one person's settings decide what thousands of other people can do
  • A real design partnership. You write problem briefs rather than solutions, you can say why a design is good and not just whether you like it, and you have changed a designer's mind and had yours changed
  • Comfort going deep with engineers on architecture and tradeoffs, then explaining them clearly to customers and executives
  • A standing customer cadence you own, not research handed to you. You can point to a time a customer insight reversed a plan you had already made
  • Explicit prioritization. You can walk through a real sequencing decision: the criteria you used, what you consciously dropped, and who was unhappy about it
  • You enjoy envisioning the big picture and managing the details
  • Strong written and verbal communication. You lead with the recommendation, make the tradeoff explicit, and keep it short enough that people actually read it
  • You like getting your hands dirty and getting out in the field to understand customer pain points

Employee Benefits

Verkada is committed to fostering a workplace environment that prioritizes the holistic health and wellbeing of our employees and their families by offering comprehensive wellness perks, benefits, and resources. Our benefits and perks programs include, but are not limited to:

  • Healthcare programs that can be tailored to meet the personal health and financial well-being needs - Premiums are 100% covered for the employee under at least one plan and 80% for family premiums under all plans
  • Nationwide medical, vision and dental coverage
  • Starting January 2027, Verkada will match a portion of an employee’s 401(k) contributions based on eligible earnings. Match vests on 2 year anniversary
  • Health Saving Account (HSA) with annual employer contributions and Flexible Spending Account (FSA) with tax saving options
  • Expanded mental health support
  • Paid parental leave policy & fertility benefits
  • Time off to relax and recharge through our paid holidays, firmwide extended holidays, flexible PTO and personal sick time
  • Professional development stipend
  • Wellness/fitness benefits
  • Healthy lunches provided daily
  • Commuter benefits

Additional Information:

  • We do sponsor and take over sponsorship of employment visas for this role. If we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa.

Annual Pay Range

At Verkada, we want to attract and retain the best employees, and compensate them in a way that appropriately and fairly values their individual contribution to the company. With that in mind, we carefully consider a number of factors to determine the appropriate starting pay for an employee, including their primary work location and an assessment of a candidate's skills and experience, as well as market demands and internal parity. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Sentry Software (Manufacturing)
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The Sentry Tower Software team is responsible for developing robotic systems that provide force protection capabilities, monitoring the perimeter of secure areas, land or sea, for approaching people, vehicles, and vessels. We live in a world where security officers are increasingly overwhelmed by sensor data feeds. Our products leverage advanced sensor fusion and autonomy to seamlessly render activity in the environment to Lattice's common operating picture.

About the Job

We are looking for a Software Engineer with a focus in Manufacturing to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa. In this role you will be responsible for building and maintaining software for current and next generation Sentry Tower systems. You will be responsible for developing automated test suites and user-friendly interfaces to streamline hardware verification and issue diagnosis for non-technical users. You will implement robust error-capturing mechanisms that provide actionable insights for efficient troubleshooting and quality assurance.

Every tower we ship passes through this software. It is what proves a unit works before it leaves the floor, which makes it the last chance to catch a defect while the hardware is still in reach and the fix costs an hour instead of a trip to a site. A test that passes when it should not have is the most expensive kind of bug we have, because it ships.

The honest version: your users are technicians on a production floor, not engineers, and their time is the constraint. That means a lot of the work is unglamorous by design: clear error messages, tooling that fails in an obvious way, and diagnostics a person can follow at 6am without calling you. You will also be pulled into whatever is blocking the line, which does not wait for your sprint. The upside is a feedback loop most software engineers never get, since the people using what you built are in the same building and will tell you within a day.

Our Product: https://www.anduril.com/hardware/sentry/

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Develop automated test suites to verify hardware functionality and performance.
  • Create user-friendly interfaces to facilitate issue diagnosis for non-technical users.
  • Implement robust error-capturing mechanisms to provide actionable insights.
  • Collaborate with hardware and quality assurance teams to ensure seamless integration of testing tools.
  • Work directly with the technicians and manufacturing engineers who use your tooling every shift, and treat their time as the thing you are optimizing.
  • Continuously improve testing frameworks to enhance efficiency and reliability.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience building test automation, instrumentation, or tooling for hardware, and comfort working on a bench with the hardware in front of you.
  • Proficiency in Python for test and tooling work, plus 2+ years in Rust or C++ to work in the services under test.
  • Solid grasp of networking principles, including CAN and Ethernet protocols, along with expertise in hardware interfacing, diagnostic tools (e.g., Wireshark, CANoe), and cybersecurity principles as they pertain to secure and reliable sensor data transmission.
  • Strong engineering background from industry or school, ideally in areas/fields such as Computer Science, Software Engineering, Mathematics, or Physics.
  • US person status required, with eligibility to obtain and maintain a US security clearance.

About Redwood Materials

Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. Position Summary: 

The Senior Battery Systems Engineer leads the cross-functional integration of new OEM battery packs into the stationary energy storage system architecture within the Energy Storage engineering function. The role independently owns the system architecture, requirements, and interface definitions for each integrated pack, aligning mechanical, electrical, controls, power electronics, and software engineering on a common technical baseline. This role serves as the technical point of contact for external OEMs and suppliers on pack-level integration, adapting automotive packs to off-vehicle duty cycles with limited precedent. The position is reviewed at critical design decision points and is accountable for system-level requirements being complete, testable, and verified. This is a fully on-site role at 100 Hooper, with occasional travel to sites and vendors.

  • Leads cross-functional integration of new OEM battery packs from technical intake through validation and deployment
  • Owns system-level architecture, performance, and functional requirements for integrated packs and derives subsystem and component requirements with design engineers
  • Defines and maintains mechanical, electrical, communication, and software interfaces between OEM packs and the energy storage system
  • Leads technical discussions with OEMs and suppliers to obtain pack data, resolve integration issues, and agree on engineering solutions
  • Leads DFMEAs, hazard analyses, and risk assessments for integrated packs and tracks mitigations to closure
  • Ensures integrated systems comply with applicable UL and industry standards 

Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities  

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field and 5+ years of systems or design engineering experience, or a Master's degree and 3+ years
  • Working knowledge of lithium-ion battery pack architecture, battery management systems, and pack communication protocols (CAN, Modbus, Ethernet)
  • Experience with energy storage systems, hybrid or electric powertrain development, or PV system development
  • Ability to write clear, testable engineering requirements and manage them in a requirements management tool

We are looking for a deeply technical, hands-on Battery Software & Controls Integration Engineer who lives at the intersection of electrochemistry, embedded BMS firmware, and high-voltage pack hardware. 

In this role, you won't just write high-level communication wrappers—you will get your hands dirty in the lab bringing up heterogeneous OEM battery packs off-vehicle, reverse-engineering proprietary BMS architectures, and validating the underlying battery state estimation algorithms.   • Technical OEM & Supplier Leadership: Serve as the primary technical counterpart to external automotive OEMs and Tier-1 BMS suppliers. Drive deep-dive engineering reviews to negotiate custom passive-monitor BMS firmware builds, extract charge/discharge lookup tables, understand pyrotechnic disconnect/fuse curves, and establish deterministic command hooks. 
  • SIL/HIL & Physical Hardware Verification: Partner with validation and power electronics teams to model pack dynamics, inject sensor and contactor faults on HIL benches (Typhoon HIL/Opal-RT) and physical cyclers, and verify functional safety boundaries before field deployment.

jobs.description:

Position Summary

The Lead Project Controls Specialist serves as a project controls lead for Redwood’s EPC capital projects, owning the integrated cost and schedule baseline and the performance reporting that leadership relies on to make decisions. This role develops and tracks project KPIs, administers earned value management, and leads cost control, budget tracking, forecasting, and change management across engineering, procurement, and construction phases. The successful candidate will set project controls standards and procedures, provide technical direction and mentorship to schedulers, and act as the primary controls interface with EPC contractors, project management, and Finance.

Responsibilities/Essential Duties will Include:

  • Lead the project controls function for assigned capital projects, setting the standards, procedures, and reporting cadence used across cost, schedule, estimating, and change management.
  • Develop, structure, and maintain the project work breakdown structure (WBS), along with the supporting cost breakdown structure (CBS) and organizational breakdown structure (OBS), so that scope, schedule activities, estimates, commitments, and actual costs all map to a single coding framework and roll up cleanly at any level of the project.
  • Develop, baseline, and maintain the project KPI set — including CPI, SPI, productivity factors, commodity installation curves, safety and quality leading indicators, and milestone adherence — and track performance against targets throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Own earned value management for the project: establish control accounts and work packages against the WBS, define rules of credit and progress measurement methods, and calculate and analyze BCWS, BCWP, ACWP, CV, SV, EAC, ETC, and TCPI.
  • Govern the integrity of the WBS and coding structures over the project lifecycle — aligning them with ERP/accounting cost codes, and estimate structures, and controlling revisions as scope and contracting strategy evolve.
  • Direct cost control activities, including budget development and allocation, commitment and expenditure tracking, accruals, cash flow projections, and monthly cost forecasts at the control account and project level.
  • Build and maintain the project budget, track actuals against budget, and produce variance analyses that explain cost and schedule deviations, quantify their impact, and identify corrective actions.
  • Manage the change control process — evaluating trends, change orders, and scope revisions for cost and schedule impact, maintaining the change log and contingency/management reserve registers, and ensuring approved changes are incorporated into the baseline.
  • Develop, integrate, and maintain cost-loaded and resource-loaded schedules in Primavera P6, including critical path analysis, schedule health checks, and progress updates from field and contractor data.
  • Produce and present weekly and monthly project performance reports and executive dashboards, translating cost, schedule, and earned value data into clear findings and recommendations for project and senior leadership.
  • Perform quantitative risk analysis, including schedule and cost risk assessments, what-if and recovery scenario modeling, and contingency drawdown tracking.
  • Partner with Finance, Procurement, Engineering, Estimating, and Construction Management to align project reporting with capital budgets, purchase commitments, and accounting periods.
  • Establish and improve project controls tools, templates, data structures, and reporting automation to increase accuracy and reduce manual reporting effort.
  • Provide guidance, training, and technical mentorship to planners, schedulers, and cost analysts, and review their work products for quality and consistency.
  • Support project close-out, including final cost reconciliation, schedule performance analysis, benchmarking, and capture of lessons learned and historical data for future estimates.

 

  • Desired Qualifications:
  • Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering, business administration, or a related field. Equivalent work experience may be considered.
  • Minimum of 8 years of project controls experience on construction, EPC, or large-scale industrial capital projects, including time in a lead or senior role directing controls scope and personnel.
  • Demonstrated ownership of cost control, budget tracking, and forecasting on projects of significant capital value, from baseline development through close-out.
  • Hands-on expertise in earned value management, including progress measurement, rules of credit, control account structures, and EAC/ETC forecasting.
  • Proven experience developing project KPIs and building performance reports and dashboards for project and executive audiences.
  • Advanced proficiency in Primavera P6; experience with cost management systems (e.g., EcoSys, Oracle, SAP) and reporting tools such as Power BI or Tableau.
  • Advanced Excel skills for cost modeling, data analysis, and reconciliation of large data sets.
  • Demonstrated experience structuring WBS, CBS, and OBS for large capital projects, including control account design, cost coding, and alignment of contractor and ERP reporting structures.
  • Strong working knowledge of change management, trend programs, and contingency and risk management practices.
  • Experience with quantitative schedule and cost risk analysis and what-if scenario modeling.
  • Experience reviewing contractor progress claims, invoices, and baseline schedules, and supporting negotiation of change orders and delay claims.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain cost and schedule performance to technical and non-technical stakeholders and to influence without direct authority.
  • AACE (CCP, EVP, PSP) or PMI (PMP, PMI-SP) certification preferred.
  • Experience in battery, chemical processing, heavy manufacturing, or other complex industrial environments is a plus.

 

The position is full-time. Compensation will be commensurate with experience.

jobs.description:
About Carvana

At Carvana, we’re changing the way people buy and sell cars. With an ambitious vision and a fundamentally different approach designed to be fun, fast, and fair, Carvana became the fastest-growing automotive retailer in history. We expanded nationally, went public on the New York Stock Exchange, sold our 1 millionth car, and reached the Fortune 500, all in just eight years.

Today, with 4 million retail customers and counting, Carvana is both the fastest-growing and the most profitable public automotive retailer, and we’re just getting started. We continue to raise the bar for our customers as we tackle the enormous opportunity still ahead in the largest consumer vertical.

Working here means being part of a team that embraces change, celebrates creative problem solving, and always strives to be better. At Carvana, you’ll have the opportunity to take on meaningful challenges, learn quickly, and help shape the future of automotive retail. If you’re driven to grow and make an impact as part of a collaborative team, you’ll fit right in. Learn more about what it’s like to work here from the people that already do. 

Work Model: This is a 100% on-site role at our Tempe office, Monday through Friday.

About the team and position

We’re looking for an experienced Senior Engineer, Information Security to join our internal Security Operations Team. While this team is responsible for monitoring, detecting, and reporting cyber threats, your role will be a force multiplier.

You will lead the design and implementation of automated response actions, build next-generation AI-assisted workflows, and develop custom integrations  You will evangelize automation and the adoption of AI across the broader Technology Services organization.

What you’ll be doing

  • Design, build, and maintain automated security playbooks and workflows using Torq or similar SOAR platforms to automate incident response and manual tasks.
  • Develop AI-assisted workflows and integrate Large Language Models (LLMs) into security processes to accelerate decision-making and analysis.
  • Develop custom scripts and integrations (using Python, REST APIs, etc.) to bridge gaps between disparate security tools and enterprise systems.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to ensure appropriate logs and data are ingested effectively to support automation logic.
  • Evangelize automation across the broader Technology Services organization.
  • Build and implement automation and AI agents to support the broader technology organization. 
  • Identify opportunities to automate manual, repetitive security tasks to free up analyst time for higher-value threat hunting.
  • Apply software development best practices (version control, testing, code review) to security operations.
  • Work with vendors to develop technical solutions to mitigate security vulnerabilities and automate tasks.
  • Create and/or document standards and operating procedures for automation architecture.
  • Stay abreast of security news and emerging AI technologies to offer innovative automation solutions that mitigate potential risks.
  • Be an integral member of projects teams that is responsible for the secure architecture of Carvana systems. 
  • Consult and provide security requirements and recommendations for ongoing projects and new system implementations. 
  • Take a risk based approach at reviewing systems or applications that do not meet security requirements or security policies and writing security exceptions when required. 
  • Resolve security related tasks from a ticketing queue.
  • Occasionally serve as Tier 3 support for alerts that are monitored by the Security Operations Center.
  • Work with vendors to bring solutions to resolve current security issues and/or develop technical solutions to mitigate security vulnerabilities and automate tasks.
  • Create and/or document standards and operating procedures. 
  • Train junior members and members of other teams on Information Security.
  • Stay abreast of security news that could have an impact on the security of Carvana and offer solutions to mitigate potential risks. 
  • This role involves being on an on-call rotation for after hours and weekend support. 

What you should have

  • 5+ years of experience in security engineering or software development.
  • Proven experience with SOAR platforms (e.g., Torq, Splunk SOAR/Phantom, Cortex XSOAR, Swimlane).
  • Strong proficiency in scripting and software development languages (e.g., Python) for API integration and data processing.
  • Experience designing AI-driven automation or integrating AI/LLM capabilities into operational workflows.
  • Deep understanding of RESTful APIs and experience integrating various security tools (SIEM, EDR, Firewalls, etc.).
  • Experience working in a Security Operations Center (SOC) and understanding Incident Response lifecycles.
  • Technical proficiency in MITRE ATT&CK framework and strong understanding of current attack vectors.
  • Proven experience in securing a complex, diverse, distributed technology footprint.

What we’ll offer in return

  • Full-Time Salary Position with a competitive salary.
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits.
  • 401K with company match.
  • A multitude of perks including student loan payments, discounts on vehicles, benefits for your pets, and much more.
  • A great wellness program to keep you healthy and happy both physically and mentally.
  • Access to training and conference opportunities as well as great on-the-job training.
  • A company culture of promotions from within, with a start-up atmosphere allowing for varied and rapid career development.
  • A seat in one of the fastest-growing companies in the country.

Other requirements

To be able to do your job at Carvana, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you.

  • Must be able to read, write, speak, and understand English.
  • Requires excellent visual acuity and manual dexterity.

Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs. 

Legal stuff

Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check.  This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

Carvana is an equal employment opportunity employer.  All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, age, mental or physical disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law.  Carvana also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories.

jobs.title: Staff BESS Electrical Design Engineer, EPC
jobs.description:
About Redwood Materials

Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. On the energy side, Redwood has deployed the largest second-life battery project in the world, delivering power to AI data centers in months rather than years using proprietary energy architecture engineered entirely in-house. The company is profitable, the market it operates in is projected to grow 20 to 50 times over the next decade, and Redwood is the only company with the supply chain, the technology, and the operational scale to lead it.

Staff BESS Electrical Design Engineer, EPC

Redwood Materials is seeking a Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) Electrical Engineer to join our EPC team. This role is central to the design of scalable, high-performance energy storage infrastructure for utility-scale and distributed applications. Our mission is to build a sustainable circular economy for lithium-ion batteries by transforming recycled materials into high-quality inputs for new batteries.

Responsibilities will include: 

  • Lead electrical engineering efforts for utility scale lithium-ion BESS projects from concept (system sizing, layout) through construction. 
  • Interface with utilities and ISO/RTOs to support interconnection studies/submittals, permitting, and compliance for new renewable and BESS projects. 
  • Serve as the internal subject matter expert (SME) for technical challenges related to BESS.  
  • Design AC and DC electrical systems for BESS using medium voltage transformers, inverters, DC combiners, energy managers, and battery modules. Specify and procure long-lead AC equipment. 
  • Develop schematic diagrams, single-line diagrams, wiring schematics, raceway plans, grounding plans, and protection strategies for AC and DC systems. 
  • Specify and evaluate components such as circuit breakers, contactors, fuses, disconnects, emergency power off (EPO), and metering devices. 
  • Coordinate with civil, structural, fire & life safety, SCADA/telecom, geotechnical, and DC system design teams to produce complete IFC packages and technical specifications. 
  • Ensure designs comply with applicable codes and standards such as NEC 705, NEC 706, IEEE 1547, UL 9540, NFPA 855, and local amendments. Lead code reviews and provide summary to internal teams. 
  • Integration of BESS with grid infrastructure and other renewable and traditional energy sources.  
  • Perform power system studies for short circuit, load flow, arc flash, and protective device coordination for AC and DC systems. 
  • Serve as the Electrical Engineer of Record for assigned projects. 
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of BESS technologies, codes, and industry trends.  
  • Lead R&D efforts to perform feasibility analysis of using medium voltage DC distribution system for integrating BESS with other sources. 
  • Provide CA support for RFIs, submittal reviews, change orders, and site inspections. 
  • Coordinate with internal stakeholders and external consultants to track scope, schedule, and budget. 
  • Prepare engineering cost estimates and project schedules in collaboration with project controls at various design milestones. 
  • Perform QA/QC reviews of electrical designs and mentor junior engineers. 
  • Contribute to internal design standards, templates, and best practices. 
  • Manage project workload and ensure timely delivery of engineering documents. 
  • Support strategic initiatives related to grid integration, renewable energy, and energy storage. 

Desired Qualifications: 

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering from ABET accredited program.

Battery Disassembly Technician, Energy Storage 

The Battery Disassembly Technician performs safe, efficient, and high-quality disassembly of EV battery packs and modules within a high-volume manufacturing environment. The position requires strict adherence to high-voltage safety protocols, standardized work instructions, and continuous process improvement. 

Responsibilities will include:

  • Perform safe, controlled disassembly of EV and energy storage battery packs down to module and component level, following detailed work instructions and safety standards
  • Execute high-voltage isolation, verification, and handling procedures, including strict adherence to lockout/tagout (LOTO) and PPE requirements
  • Sort, classify, and route battery components for reuse, recycling, or disposal in compliance with environmental and production guidelines
  • Operate within a high-throughput production environment, meeting performance targets while maintaining efficiency, accuracy, and workflow continuity
  • Utilize hand tools, power tools, and electrical diagnostic equipment to support disassembly, inspection, and basic troubleshooting tasks
  • Safely handle, transport, and lift large-format battery systems using forklifts, cranes, hoists, and rigging equipment in accordance with safety protocols
  • Collaborate cross-functionally to support continuous improvement, maintain a safe and organized workspace, and ensure compliance with quality and EHS standards

Desired Qualifications:

  • Operate a variety of material handling equipment and mechanical lifts (training provided). 
  • Must meet all requirements for use of a full-face respirator, including medical clearance and fit testing, in accordance with OSHA and company standards. 
  • Demonstrates working knowledge of mechanical fastening systems, electrical connections, and component-level disassembly techniques. 
  • Prior rigging and heavy material handling experience is strongly preferred; however, training and certification will be provided for candidates with foundational mechanical aptitude. 
  • Supports field operations as required (up to 10% travel) for battery system decommissioning, including on-site disassembly and material recovery. 
  • Position includes additional internal and external trainings such as LOTO, Lifting/Rigging and High voltage Battery Basics etc. 
  • A Passion for sustainability and making the world a better place!

 

The position is full-time. Compensation will be commensurate with experience.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Sentry Software (Ground Based Air Defense)
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The Sentry Tower Software team develops robotic systems that provide force protection capabilities, monitoring the perimeter of secure areas, land or sea, for approaching people, vehicles, and vessels. We live in a world where security officers are increasingly overwhelmed by sensor data feeds. Our products leverage advanced sensor fusion and autonomy to seamlessly render activity in the environment to Lattice's common operating picture.

About the Job

Not every Sentry Tower does the same job. The same core platform that watches a perimeter for people and vehicles also underpins our ground-based air defense variants, where the tower's mission is detecting and tracking aircraft, and the sensor payload, the radar integration, and the configuration all shift accordingly. We're hiring a Software Engineer to develop and own the software for those variants, funded by and delivered to our Air Defense program. The threat they exist for is the cheap, fast, hard-to-see aircraft that has changed what defending a fixed site means. Detection has to happen with enough time left to do something about it, which puts the burden on how well the payload, the tracking, and the configuration actually work together on a real tower.

You will work in the same declarative NixOS platform the rest of the team builds on, owning your variants' slice of it: product configuration, radar and camera payload integration, networking, manufacturing test hooks, and the software update path. Some of this is new feature work driven by program requirements, and some of it is consolidation, because these variant configurations grew up separately from our modern platform base, and moving them onto it means understanding both well enough to prove nothing was lost in the move. This program delivers several products, a few of them tower variants, and those variants are what you'll work on. The result is that you end up knowing how they are put together better than anyone, which is genuinely useful to a team this size.

This is a good role for an engineer who wants breadth. You'll touch the radar and camera services, the network configuration, the build system, and the manufacturing and field tooling, with an experienced team around you owning each of those domains in depth. Travel is light, roughly 10% and mostly local, to test sites and the manufacturing floor rather than overseas.

The honest shape of the role: the scope is the program's tower variants rather than the whole product line, and the schedule comes substantially from the contract rather than from what you would pick next. Most days are integration work, configuration, and support rather than novel algorithms. What you get in exchange is unusual breadth and products you own end to end. If you want to go deep on one technical specialty, this is not that role.

Our Product: https://www.anduril.com/sentry

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own the software configuration for the Air Defense tower variants: product definitions, payload and sensor configuration, networking, and image builds in our declarative platform.
  • Integrate and support the variants' sensor payloads, particularly radar and infrared camera services, including the configuration and behavior differences that separate them from our perimeter security products.
  • Develop features driven by Air Defense program requirements, working from program needs through design, implementation, and delivery into a shipping product.
  • Migrate the variants' legacy configuration onto our modern platform base, replacing product-specific one-offs with the common, composable modules the rest of the fleet uses.
  • Own the variants' software update and deployment path, and the manufacturing test configuration that validates units as they're built.
  • Support the product in the field and on the line: triage issues, reproduce and root-cause them, fix what's yours, and drive what isn't with the owning team.
  • Work with the Air Defense program's engineers and stakeholders to keep requirements, schedule, and technical reality aligned.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering building and shipping real systems.
  • Proficiency in Rust or C++, with the ability to work across an existing codebase you didn't write.
  • Solid Linux systems fundamentals: the command line, systemd, networking basics, and log-driven debugging.
  • Practical experience integrating software with hardware, whether sensors, embedded devices, or instrumentation, and comfort working on a bench with real equipment.
  • Demonstrated ability to own a piece of a larger system end to end, including the unglamorous parts: configuration, deployment, testing, and support.
  • Clear written communication, since you'll be the interface between a program's requirements and the team's implementation.
  • US person status required, with eligibility to obtain and maintain a US security clearance.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience with radar, RF systems, or air surveillance and tracking.
  • Experience with camera or imaging pipelines, especially infrared.
  • Experience with declarative configuration management or infrastructure-as-code. Nix or NixOS is what we use; adjacent tooling is a fine starting point.
  • Python for tooling, scripting, and test automation.
  • Robotics experience, or work with motion control and pointing systems.
US Salary Range
$167,000—$222,000 USD

Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

    • Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

jobs.title: Staff Hardware Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
Everpure (NYSE: P) has evolved from storage pioneer to data platform, closing fiscal 2026 with $3.7 billion in revenue, its first billion-dollar quarter, and accelerating growth into FY27. Our strategic agenda spans the companies defining the next era of technology - hyperscalers, AI labs, the AI hardware supply chain, data platform providers, and the broader AI ecosystem.

This type of work—work that changes the world—is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

 

THE ROLE

Drive the hardware engineering lifecycle for Everpure’s Hyperscale Line of Business, shaping high-performance, energy-efficient storage architectures tailored directly to hyperscale partners. You will serve as the technical lead bridging customer requirements and internal engineering execution, ensuring custom hardware solutions meet exacting performance and total cost of ownership (TCO) benchmarks. Working closely with cross-functional teams in validation, diagnostics, manufacturing test, and operations, you will lead hardware qualification projects, solve critical escalations, and advance system robustness. This role gives you direct ownership over the hardware that powers next-generation, large-scale data infrastructure.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Lead Hardware Qualification & System Hardening: Plan, execute, and automate comprehensive x86 hardware validation cycles—including electrical, signal integrity, and protocol testing—to guarantee system reliability for enterprise hyperscale deployments.

  • Drive Cross-Functional Production Readiness: Partner with operations, manufacturing test, and software diagnostic teams to transition custom storage subsystems into full-scale production, establishing clear test coverage and automated validation workflows.

  • Resolve High-Impact Technical Escalations: Perform root-cause analysis on complex hardware failures and field escalations, using advanced tools like high-speed oscilloscopes and bus analyzers to trace and rectify system-level anomalies.

  • Optimize Subsystem Efficiency & Architecture: Evaluate and select critical hardware components—such as CPU subsystems, DDR4/5 memory, PCIe devices, BMCs, and power distribution modules—to optimize energy efficiency and system performance.

  • Mentor and Elevate Engineering Standards: Provide technical guidance and mentorship to engineering peers, refining qualification processes and stress-testing methodologies (using tools like PTU, Mprime, and Iometer) to continuously improve team output.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • Hardware Engineering Expertise: Advanced technical mastery in x86 architectures, enterprise storage systems, subcomponent selection (NVMe, power supplies, PWM design), and high-speed bus interfaces (PCIe, SAS/SATA, UPI, I2C/I3C, SPI).

  • Validation & Automation Capability: Proven ability to design, automate, and execute hardware qualification frameworks using scripting languages (such as Python or BASH) alongside industry-standard stress and diagnostic tools.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Sentry Software (Allied Customer Deployment)
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The Sentry Tower Software team develops robotic systems that provide force protection capabilities, monitoring the perimeter of secure areas, land or sea, for approaching people, vehicles, and vessels. We live in a world where security officers are increasingly overwhelmed by sensor data feeds. Our products leverage advanced sensor fusion and autonomy to seamlessly render activity in the environment to Lattice's common operating picture.

About the Job

Sentry Towers protect perimeters for allied partner nations as well as US customers, and those deployments are their own engineering problem. A partner program brings its own site conditions, its own communications and network environment, its own integration requirements, and its own operators, and none of it is solved by shipping the standard configuration and hoping. We're hiring a Software Engineer dedicated to one such program: making our towers work for that customer, in their environment, and keeping them working. This is a customer with no second system to fall back on. When a tower is down, the perimeter it was watching is being watched by people instead, and the fix depends on an engineer who understands both our software and their site.

This is a hands-on integration and support role rather than a pure feature-development one. You will own the software configuration for this program's towers, built on our declarative NixOS platform: product configuration, network integration into the customer's environment, payload and sensor setup, and the deployment and update path for systems in the customer's hands. When something doesn't work in the field, you're the engineer who reproduces it, root-causes it, and either fixes it or drives the fix with the team that owns the component.

Expect meaningful travel, roughly 30% of your time, much of it extended international trips for installation, integration, and operator support. Some of it is not optional: when a program milestone depends on being on site, you'll be on site. The compensation for that is direct contact with the people using what you build. You will watch an operator use your work, learn things no bug report would have told you, and carry them back.

Worth weighing honestly before you apply. This is reactive work by nature: your week can get reorganized by what broke, and the roadmap you planned on Monday is not always the one you follow. You will go deep on one program rather than broad across the product, which builds unusually specific expertise and means your work is harder to point at than a shipped feature. Time zones will cost you: some of the coordination happens early, some late, and it is not evenly distributed. People take this role and love it, and people take it and find out they wanted to be writing features. Both are worth knowing about yourself first.

Our Product: https://www.anduril.com/sentry

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own the software configuration for this program's tower variants in our declarative platform, from product definitions through payload and sensor configuration to image builds.
  • Integrate towers into the customer's network and communications environment, covering addressing, routing, backhaul, and any interfaces the program requires.
  • Own the deployment and software update path for the program's fielded systems, including provisioning, staged rollout, and verification that an update landed cleanly.
  • Travel to customer sites for installation, integration, commissioning, and operator support, including extended international deployments, at approximately 30% of your time.
  • Be the program's technical front line: triage field issues, reproduce them on a bench or in simulation, root-cause them, and either fix them directly or drive the fix with the owning team.
  • Build the tooling, documentation, and runbooks that let field personnel and the customer's own operators resolve routine problems without escalating.
  • Represent the program back into engineering, making sure customer requirements and field realities reach the teams whose roadmaps need to reflect them.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering, with time spent on systems that are deployed and operated rather than only developed.
  • Solid Linux systems skills: the command line, systemd, log analysis, and the ability to diagnose a misbehaving service on a machine you didn't set up.
  • Practical networking competence: addressing and subnetting, routing, DNS, VLANs, and packet capture, enough to integrate a system into someone else's network and debug it when it doesn't come up.
  • Proficiency in at least one of Python, Rust, C++, or Go, and willingness to work in Rust and C++ where our services live.
  • Willingness and ability to travel approximately 30% of the time, including extended international trips that cannot be rescheduled around, and to work effectively on customer sites.
  • Strong written communication and follow-through, since much of this role is coordinating across time zones and leaving behind documentation someone else depends on.
  • US person status required. Active US Secret clearance, or a previously granted Secret clearance eligible for reactivation.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience with declarative configuration management or infrastructure-as-code. Nix or NixOS is what we use; adjacent tooling is a fine starting point.
  • Field service, field engineering, or deployment engineering background, especially on hardware systems.
  • Experience integrating with radios, satellite terminals, cellular backhaul, or constrained and intermittent network links.
  • Prior work supporting international or defense customers, or in a program-facing engineering role.
  • Additional language skills, or experience working with non-native-English-speaking operators and partner engineering teams.
  • Familiarity with robotics, sensor systems, cameras, or radar.

Every Sentry Tower we ship, across Counter-Intrusion and Air Defense, boots from a common software platform: a NixOS-based overlay that defines the base images, the system services, the compute configuration for each hardware generation, and the network topology that ties the tower’s payloads together. That platform is the foundation the entire product line stands on, and we are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to own it.

This is a systems and infrastructure role with unusually direct product consequences. The tower’s network is not a datacenter network: it is a set of VLANs and bridges carrying camera, radar, GPS, and sensor-board traffic over a mix of mesh radio, cellular, and satellite backhaul, on hardware that sits at the far end of a very long support loop. When a business line adds a new payload with its own switch, or when a routing priority is wrong, the failure shows up in the field. You will own the topology as a contract: define it, document it, review changes against it, and make the correct integration the easy one.

You will also be a primary steward of our build and configuration system. Our images are fully declarative and reproducible, spanning several compute generations and a dozen product variants, and we are actively consolidating legacy per-product configurations into a common, composable base.

Our Product: https://www.anduril.com/sentry

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own the shared base of our NixOS overlay: system modules, compute platform definitions, common tower services, and the image definitions that every product variant composes from.
  • Own the tower network topology end to end: VLAN and subnet allocation, bridging, link ranking and failover across heterogeneous backhaul, NAT and firewall policy, and the physical-port-to-payload mapping for each carrier board.
  • Define and enforce the integration contract that business line teams use to add network-attached payloads, so their additions extend the platform instead of diverging from it.
  • Drive the consolidation of legacy, per-product configurations into the common overlay, with build-time checks that keep them from drifting back apart.
  • Support and extend our real-time messaging layer as services migrate from the legacy pub-sub bus to its next-generation replacement, including the topic and schema contracts that define who owns which data.
  • Debug problems that cross every layer at once: kernel and device tree, systemd unit ordering, Nix evaluation, link-layer configuration, and the sensor daemons on top.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 4+ years of professional software engineering with substantial time in Linux systems, embedded platforms, or infrastructure work.
  • Deep, practical networking knowledge: VLANs, bridging, routing and policy routing, DHCP, multicast, NAT, and firewalling, plus fluency with ip, tcpdump, and Wireshark for diagnosing real traffic.
  • Strong experience with declarative configuration management and reproducible builds. Nix or NixOS is what we use and what we most want to see; adjacent depth in Bazel, Buildroot, Yocto, or infrastructure-as-code tooling (Terraform, Ansible, Pulumi) is a solid substitute.
  • Proficiency in Rust or C++, enough to read and modify the services that sit on top of the platform, not just the configuration that deploys them.
  • Comfort operating and troubleshooting real hardware: serial consoles, provisioning and reflashing, boot problems, and remote debugging of systems you cannot physically reach.
  • Demonstrated ability to define a technical interface that other teams build against, and to hold that line through code review and documentation rather than authority.
  • US person status required, with eligibility to obtain and maintain a US security clearance.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Hands-on NixOS experience, including writing modules and maintaining flakes.
  • Python for tooling and automation.
  • Experience with NVIDIA Jetson platforms (Xavier, Orin, Thor) including BSP integration, device trees, and JetPack upgrades.
  • Fleet-scale operational experience: over-the-air update systems, observability pipelines, or long-lived embedded deployments.
  • Familiarity with CAN, SNMP, or managed-switch configuration in an embedded context.
  • Experience setting up and maintaining CI/CD for large build graphs and hardware-in-the-loop pipelines.

$167,000—$222,000 USD

jobs.description:
