jobs.title: Director, Powered Land Development
jobs.description:
About Redwood Materials

Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. On the energy side, Redwood has deployed the largest second-life battery project in the world, delivering power to AI data centers in months rather than years using proprietary energy architecture engineered entirely in-house. The company is profitable, the market it operates in is projected to grow 20 to 50 times over the next decade, and Redwood is the only company with the supply chain, the technology, and the operational scale to lead it.

Position Summary: 

The Director, Powered Land Development is responsible for building Redwood Materials' powered land development function from the ground up: sourcing, evaluating, and advancing sites for Redwood Energy's solar and storage deployments. This role will focus on site selection, permitting and entitlements, local stakeholder and community engagement, and in some cases, interconnection and utility queue management. The role independently screens and diligences a wide range of prospective sites across target markets, negotiates site control with landowners and land agents, and builds the financial models, tracking tools, and repeatable processes needed to convert land opportunities into bankable, executable projects. Success depends on sound judgment operating with substantial ambiguity, comfort representing Redwood with landowners, counsel, and local officials, and the ability to build and lead the powered land development function while partnering closely with Engineering, Finance, and Legal. 

Responsibilities 

  • Source, screen, and evaluate prospective sites for Redwood Energy's solar and storage deployments across target markets, including land use, zoning, and site-level fatal-flaw analysis 
  • Lead entitlement and permitting strategy, engaging local, county, and state officials, community stakeholders, and land agents to advance project feasibility 
  • Support government affairs and community relations efforts tied to prospective sites 
  • Negotiate and secure site control (leases, easements, options, and related agreements) with landowners and land agents 
  • Represent Redwood with landowners, brokers, customers, and state and local officials throughout the site-selection process, including leading and negotiating agreements for local economic development, tax, and community agreements 
  • Develop and own financial and valuation models to evaluate site economics, development costs, and project returns 
  • Build and maintain tracking tools for land inventory, pipeline status, budgets, and schedules across active development sites 
  • Manage site-identification tasks against budgets and schedules, including coordinating internal and external technical support such as environmental consultants, engineers, and outside legal counsel 
  • Maintain disciplined pipeline tracking and reporting to keep leadership informed of site status, risk, and timeline 

Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities  

  • Bachelor's degree in real estate development, engineering, business, planning, or a related field 
  • 10+ years of experience in energy project development, real estate development, or land acquisition, ideally including utility-scale solar, storage, or data center site development 
  • Demonstrated experience navigating local and county-level permitting, zoning, and entitlement processes 
  • Track record independently sourcing and negotiating site control agreements with landowners and land agents 
  • Working knowledge of financial and valuation modeling to evaluate project economics 
  • Experience engaging and building relationships with local government officials and community stakeholders 
  • Ability to independently build processes and tools for a function with limited existing infrastructure 
  • Ability to travel extensively to support site visits, diligence, and stakeholder engagement across target markets 

The position is full-time. Compensation will be commensurate with experience.

jobs.description:
About Redwood Materials

Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. On the energy side, Redwood has deployed the largest second-life battery project in the world, delivering power to AI data centers in months rather than years using proprietary energy architecture engineered entirely in-house. The company is profitable, the market it operates in is projected to grow 20 to 50 times over the next decade, and Redwood is the only company with the supply chain, the technology, and the operational scale to lead it.

Position Summary: 

Redwood is localizing a global battery supply chain that seamlessly integrates recovery, reuse, and recycling — keeping critical minerals in circulation and driving the energy transition. We're delivering low-cost and large-scale energy storage and producing battery materials in the U.S. for the first time, all from batteries we already have. The Staff Electrical Engineer, Energy Storage BoP performs and reviews balance-of-plant power system studies, specifies major electrical equipment for Redwood’s energy storage systems, and develops protection and coordination designs. This is primarily an on-site role, with the potential for a hybrid arrangement depending on the candidate’s experience level. Some travel is also expected as part of this role. 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities 

  • Perform and review balance-of-plant power system studies including load flow, short-circuit, protection coordination, DC and AC arc flash, transformer energization, motor starting, reactive power analysis, transient overvoltage, harmonic analysis, insulation coordination, grounding design, battery sizing, and auxiliary system sizing 
  • Hands-on experience with power system protection design, relay selection, settings development, and coordination studies, particularly using SEL protective relays (e.g., SEL-751, SEL-351, SEL-487E, or equivalent). 
  • Proficiency with SEL acSELerator QuickSet, relay configuration, protection logic development, and testing/commissioning of protection schemes for MV/HV electrical systems. Experience with ETAP, ASPEN, and/or Omicron test equipment is a plus. 
  • Work closely with the energy storage team to develop accurate AC and DC system models and study assumptions 
  • Develop, review, and validate protective relay coordination studies, relay settings, and configuration files 
  • Size and specify major electrical equipment including transformers, circuit breakers, switches, inverters, generators, capacitor banks, reactors, surge arresters, switchgear, current transformers, power cables, and UPS systems 
  • Create and maintain detailed power system models using ETAP, SKM, and/or EasyPower 
  • Apply industry standards, codes, and best practices to analysis results and design recommendations (IEEE, ANSI, IEC) 
  • Prepare clear engineering reports, study summaries, and design documentation for internal and external stakeholders 

Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities  

  • 5+ years of experience performing power system analysis, including protection and coordination studies 
  • MS or PhD in Electrical Engineering with specialization in power systems 
  • Strong foundation in power system analysis including fault calculations, symmetrical components, arc flash calculations, cable sizing, and protective device selection and coordination 
  • Expert proficiency in ETAP is required; experience with SKM or EasyPower is highly preferred 
  • Experience with grounding and cable ampacity analysis tools such as CYMCAP and CDEGS is preferred 
  • Working knowledge of applicable codes and standards including NEC, IEEE, and related industry practices 
  • Experience with battery energy storage systems (BESS), inverter-based generation, and/or data center electrical systems is a plus 
  • Familiarity with short circuit and protective relay software tools such as ASPEN and/or CAPE is a plus 
  • Familiarity with PSCAD and/or PSS/E is a plus 
  • Familiarity with Python for analysis automation or data processing is a plus

  • Build and maintain cloud infrastructure as code: Implement Terraform/Terragrunt modules and live environment configurations for EKS clusters, load balancers, IAM roles, and supporting AWS services.
  • Operate Kubernetes clusters: Assist in managing multi-region EKS deployments via GitOps workflows (e.g., FluxCD, ArgoCD) and Helm charts.
  • Support CI/CD pipelines: Help design, maintain, and improve shared GitLab CI/CD pipeline templates used across team repositories, embedding DevSecOps guardrails.
  • Automate operational toil: Build tooling for tasks such as container image patching, EKS AMI rotation, and automated patching cycles.
  • Manage observability: Help provision and maintain Datadog SLOs, monitors, and dashboards; participate in the team's on-call rotation responding to incidents.

  • Apply AI tools: Leverage AI-based workflows within your domain to improve project execution, infrastructure design, and debugging.

You Have:

  • 2–4 years of experience in DevOps, Platform Engineering, or Site Reliability Engineering.
  • A BS or MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience.
  • Hands-on experience with Terraform for managing cloud infrastructure.
  • Experience with Kubernetes operations and AWS services (EKS, VPC, IAM, ECR).
  • Proficiency in at least one general-purpose programming language — Go or Python preferred — for building operational automation.
  • Experience designing or maintaining CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI/CD preferred).
  • Familiarity with container image security practices and GitOps workflows.
  • A strong operational mindset with a willingness to participate in on-call rotations and incident response.

jobs.title: Staff Cathode Engineer
jobs.description:
About Redwood Materials

Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. On the energy side, Redwood has deployed the largest second-life battery project in the world, delivering power to AI data centers in months rather than years using proprietary energy architecture engineered entirely in-house. The company is profitable, the market it operates in is projected to grow 20 to 50 times over the next decade, and Redwood is the only company with the supply chain, the technology, and the operational scale to lead it.

Position Summary

As a Staff Cathode Design Engineer, you will play a leading role in the development, scale-up, and manufacturing of Cathode Active Materials (CAM), including identifying, designing, and optimizing core production technologies. These technologies are critical to scaling cost-effective, high-performing processes that meet rigorous customer specifications and quality standards. In this role, you will lead complex technical initiatives, partner closely with cross-functional teams, and establish design parameters to drive the future of our CAM technology roadmap. Success in this position requires advanced technical expertise, strong project leadership, exceptional data analysis, and the ability to manage high-impact, competing priorities in a fast-paced environment while upholding strict quality and safety standards.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Lead Process & Scale-Up Engineering: Provide senior-level technical expertise (including mass and energy balances, process flowsheets, and advanced process simulations) to identify, design, scale, and implement process technologies for CAM manufacturing.

  • Design & Execution of Experiments: Direct and conduct advanced Design of Experiments (DOE) to guide scale-up, define precise process parameter tolerances, enhance material performance, and lower manufacturing costs.

  • Vendor & Equipment Engineering: Lead interactions with equipment suppliers across conceptual design, system specs, detailed engineering, procurement, installation, and site acceptance testing.

  • Technology Roadmap & IP Creation: Drive the development of the technology roadmap to align with long-term business strategy and customer requirements. Generate intellectual property (IP) and collaborate with legal teams to draft and file patent applications.

  • Stakeholder & Business Leadership: Serve as a technical authority and advisor for commercial teams, business development, senior management, and key external partners.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Lead multi-disciplinary engineering and operations teams to solve complex, systemic process challenges and successfully translate lab/pilot findings to commercial scale.

Desired Skills/Qualifications: 

  • Education: Advanced degree (MS or PHD) in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related engineering discipline.

  • Experience: 5+ years of industrial experience in process development, scale-up, process engineering, and technical management within chemical processing or inorganic materials.

  • Technical Mastery: Deep technical expertise in inorganic materials production, powder synthesis, and chemical engineering fundamentals.

  • Process Modeling: Proven ability to perform complex process design calculations, mass/energy balances, process flow diagram (PFD/P&ID) development, and process simulation modeling.

  • Leadership & Influence: Strong track record of leading cross-functional teams, driving high-impact technical projects, and building trust across internal stakeholders and external clients.

  • Data & Communication: Outstanding data analysis capabilities and superior written and technical presentation skills.

  • Adaptability & Drive: Demonstrated ability to manage and prioritize complex initiatives in a rapidly evolving, high-growth environment, paired with a passion for clean energy and sustainability.

 

The position is full-time. Compensation will be commensurate with experience.

We collect your PI for our purposes, including performing services and operations related to your potential employment. If you have additional privacy-related questions, please contact us at privacy@redwoodmaterials.com.

jobs.description:

Smartsheet maintains certifications and attestations across SOC 2 Type II, the ISO 27001/27017/27701/22301 suite, HIPAA, and other commercial compliance frameworks—and the manual work of proving those controls quarter after quarter doesn't scale with the business. We're looking for a Sr. Security Engineer I to bring an engineering mindset to our commercial GRC program: automating control monitoring, building evidence pipelines, and reducing the audit-season scramble into a default state of readiness. You'll work hands-on with our GRC platform, cloud, and identity tooling to make control evidence collect itself wherever possible, and you'll partner closely with engineering teams to translate compliance requirements into technical control logic they can actually build against. This is a builder's role within GRC—less checklist administration, more systems thinking applied to compliance. Our approach is grounded in GRC Engineering principles: automate early and often, treat controls and their mappings as code, favor continuous assurance over periodic checks, and build compliance that engineers can consume as easily as they contribute to it.

This role reports to the Senior Director, GRC Engineering and can be based in our Bellevue, WA office or remotely from anywhere in the US where Smartsheet is a registered employer.

You Will:

  • Own control automation for SOC 2, ISO 27001/27017/27701, HIPAA, and related commercial frameworks: design and build automated evidence collection and continuous control monitoring across cloud, identity, endpoint, and SaaS systems.
  • Express controls, control tests, and cross-framework mappings as version-controlled code so they are reviewable, testable, and reusable rather than locked in a single tool's configuration.
  • Translate compliance requirements into technical control logic, workflows, and integrations, partnering with engineering, IT, and security teams to embed controls into existing systems and pipelines rather than bolting them on after the fact.
  • Shift compliance left by participating in architecture and design reviews, defining control requirements as acceptance criteria for new systems, and helping teams build compliant-by-default infrastructure.
  • Design the engineer-facing experience of compliance: self-service control status, guardrails and paved-road patterns, and compliance feedback delivered in the tools teams already use (CI/CD, Jira, Slack) rather than only in the GRC platform.
  • Evaluate whether controls actually reduce relevant risk—not just whether they exist—and propose alternative controls when a framework default doesn't fit our threat model or workload architecture.
  • Support full audit cycles end-to-end: coordinate evidence requests, populate and maintain the evidence library, respond to auditor follow-ups, and track remediation items through closure for SOC 2, ISO, and HIPAA assessments.
  • Build and maintain dashboards and reporting that give GRC and security leadership real-time visibility into control health, evidence freshness, and audit readiness across frameworks.
  • Identify and eliminate duplicate evidence-gathering effort across overlapping frameworks by mapping controls once and reusing that mapping across SOC 2, ISO, and HIPAA.
  • Diagnose the root causes of recurring control failures or stale evidence and fix the underlying process, tooling, or ownership gap rather than the symptom.
  • Partner with the GRC Team Lead and SATellite engineering to extend our internal GRC platform's control, evidence, and risk-lifecycle capabilities.

You Have:

  • 4+ years of experience in GRC engineering, security engineering, compliance automation, or IT audit support, with hands-on ownership of at least one full certification cycle (SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar).
  • Practical, hands-on experience with GRC or compliance automation platforms (Vanta, Drata, Secureframe, or a homegrown equivalent), including configuring integrations and building evidence pipelines—not just reading dashboards.
  • Experience with cloud security fundamentals (AWS/GCP/Azure IAM, logging, encryption) and how they map to control requirements.
  • Solid working knowledge of SOC 2, ISO 27001 (and ideally 27017/27701), and HIPAA control requirements, and the ability to map controls across frameworks to avoid duplicated evidence work.
  • Comfort with scripting or light development (Python, JavaScript, or similar) to build integrations, automate evidence pulls via API, or extend GRC tooling.
  • Strong written communication; you can document a control, a gap, and a remediation plan clearly enough that an external auditor and an internal engineer both understand it.
  • A stakeholder-centric mindset: you measure success by how easy it is for engineers to stay compliant, not just by how quickly GRC can produce evidence.
  • Demonstrated ability to trace a control failure or audit finding back to its root cause and drive a durable fix across teams.

jobs.title: Director, Finance Systems & ERP
jobs.description:
For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Now, in our most ambitious chapter yet, we are uniting human teams with AI agents. By orchestrating the work agents do best, automating manual tasks and uncovering insights at scale, we create the space for people to focus on what truly matters: judgment, creativity, and big thinking. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

Corporate Systems Engineering builds and operates the software platforms, integrations, and automations that power Smartsheet’s core business functions across Finance, Sales/GTM, and People & Culture. Our team owns mission-critical systems and workflows that enable how the company hires, sells, bills, pays, reports, and scales. We operate at the intersection of software engineering, enterprise platforms, and business-critical data, treating internal systems with the same rigor, reliability, and product mindset as customer-facing software.

Financial Systems Engineering owns and evolves the technology ecosystem that powers Smartsheet’s financial operations and monetization capabilities. The team is responsible for platforms including NetSuite, Coupa, Planful, Stripe, ZoneBilling, Metronome, and supporting technologies such as Avalara, along with the integrations, data, automation, and engineering capabilities that connect these platforms across the enterprise.

As Director, Finance Systems & ERP, you will lead the engineering organization responsible for Smartsheet’s financial technology ecosystem and define the long-term technical strategy for how these platforms evolve. You will own the architecture, engineering maturity, technical health, and delivery of systems supporting core financial operations, procurement, planning, payments, billing, revenue processes, and emerging monetization models.

This is a strategic and highly visible technology leadership role. You will lead major transformation initiatives including ERP modernization, billing transformation, and the evolution toward usage-based and consumption-based monetization. You will represent Corporate Systems in executive steering committees and major transformation programs, partnering closely with Finance, Accounting, Procurement, Product Engineering, Sales/GTM, Data, and other technology leaders.

You will partner closely with Product Managers across Financial Systems and Billing & Monetization to combine business and product strategy with a forward-looking technical strategy. You will be expected to challenge legacy architectures and operating models, identify opportunities to simplify and automate financial processes, and determine how modern software engineering, enterprise data, automation, and AI can improve how Finance technology operates.

You will report to the Senior Director of Corporate Systems and collaborate closely with Product and Engineering leaders across the organization.

You Will:

  • Own the technical strategy and long-term architecture for Smartsheet’s financial systems ecosystem across ERP, procurement, financial planning, payments, billing, tax, revenue processes, integrations, data, automation, and AI
  • Lead, coach, and develop the Financial Systems Engineering organization responsible for platforms including NetSuite, Coupa, Planful, Stripe, ZoneBilling, Metronome, Avalara, and associated technologies
  • Serve as the senior technology leader for NetSuite and ERP, ensuring the platform and surrounding architecture remain scalable, maintainable, secure, auditable, and aligned with the long-term needs of a complex SaaS business
  • Provide technology leadership for major Finance transformation programs, including ERP reimplementation and modernization, establishing architecture, engineering standards, technical governance, delivery practices, and long-term platform direction
  • Partner with Product Managers for Financial Systems and Billing & Monetization to translate product strategy and business priorities into technical roadmaps, architecture, investment decisions, and executable engineering plans
  • Shape the technology architecture required to support evolving SaaS monetization models, including subscription, multi-year, usage-based, consumption-based, and AI-related pricing and billing models
  • Partner across Product Engineering, Sales/GTM, Finance, and Corporate Systems to ensure pricing and packaging strategies can be represented reliably from quote and entitlement through provisioning, usage, billing, accounting, and revenue processes
  • Establish clear architectural boundaries and systems of record across CRM, product, billing, ERP, payments, tax, planning, and downstream data platforms, reducing ambiguity, duplication, and unnecessary coupling
  • Define the strategy for Finance systems data, including authoritative sources, data models, data contracts, quality, lineage, reconciliation, historical integrity, and reliable consumption by the enterprise data platform
  • Partner closely with Data Engineering and Analytics teams to integrate Financial Systems with the enterprise data lake and ensure Finance data is timely, trustworthy, well-defined, and usable for financial reporting, operational analytics, reconciliation, and AI
  • Drive stronger data quality and observability across Quote-to-Cash and Finance workflows, moving the organization from reactive reconciliation toward proactive detection and prevention of data integrity issues
  • Establish an AI strategy for Financial Systems Engineering, identifying practical opportunities to improve engineering productivity, financial operations, controls, testing, support, reconciliation, and employee experiences
  • Evaluate and introduce AI-assisted and agentic capabilities where appropriate, while ensuring financial integrity, security, auditability, human oversight, and appropriate controls for higher-risk processes
  • Develop a strategy for automated testing and quality engineering across the Finance technology stack, including regression testing, integration testing, data validation, reconciliation, and AI-assisted test generation and analysis
  • Establish modern engineering practices across enterprise platforms, including source control, peer review, CI/CD, environment management, automated testing, observability, documentation, release engineering, and operational readiness where supported by the underlying technologies
  • Determine appropriate boundaries between native SaaS configuration, platform extensibility, APIs, integrations, automation, and custom software, avoiding unnecessary customization while enabling capabilities the business requires
  • Partner with Integration Engineering to ensure critical Finance and Quote-to-Cash integrations use scalable patterns, explicit contracts, appropriate observability, resilient error handling, and well-defined operational ownership
  • Own the technical health and lifecycle of the Financial Systems portfolio, proactively addressing architectural debt, platform limitations, fragile integrations, unnecessary customization, manual processes, and recurring operational problems
  • Establish architecture reviews, technical standards, engineering metrics, platform health reviews, and other mechanisms that continuously improve the maturity of Financial Systems Engineering
  • Represent Financial Systems Engineering on executive steering committees, transformation governance forums, and major program reviews, clearly communicating architecture decisions, delivery status, risks, dependencies, investment needs, and tradeoffs
  • Provide technical leadership across implementation partners and strategic vendors, ensuring system integrators and software providers operate within Smartsheet’s architecture, engineering, security, and delivery expectations rather than allowing vendors to define the long-term architecture
  • Partner with Finance leadership, Accounting, FP&A, Procurement, Tax, Revenue, and other stakeholders to understand business strategy while maintaining clear technology ownership of architecture and engineering decisions
  • Balance delivery of major transformation programs with operational reliability, roadmap commitments, technical debt reduction, platform modernization, security, controls, and long-term engineering investments
  • Build strong partnerships across Finance, Product Engineering, Sales/GTM, Data, Security, AI & Automation, and Corporate Systems to ensure Financial Systems operate as part of a coherent enterprise architecture
  • Recruit, develop, and retain engineering talent with a combination of Finance platform expertise, software engineering capability, systems thinking, and curiosity about the future of financial technology

You Have:

  • 10+ years of progressively responsible experience across financial systems, enterprise application engineering, ERP, software engineering, systems architecture, or related technical disciplines
  • 5+ years of experience leading technical teams, including experience managing managers, senior engineers, architects, or other technical leaders
  • Deep experience with NetSuite or comparable enterprise ERP platforms, with sufficient technical depth to lead architecture, challenge implementation decisions, and establish long-term platform strategy
  • Demonstrated experience leading a major ERP implementation, reimplementation, or transformation program from architecture and design through implementation, stabilization, and ongoing evolution
  • Strong understanding of financial business processes including record-to-report, procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, billing, payments, financial planning, accounting, and revenue-related workflows
  • Experience with financial platforms such as Coupa, Planful, Stripe, ZoneBilling, Metronome, Avalara, or comparable ERP, procurement, planning, payments, billing, tax, or monetization technologies
  • Experience with SaaS billing and monetization architectures, including subscription and usage-based or consumption-based business models
  • Strong systems thinking and the ability to reason across ERP, CRM, product, billing, payments, integrations, data platforms, APIs, automation, and financial controls as a connected architecture
  • Demonstrated experience defining technical strategy and architecture, rather than solely managing enterprise application delivery, configuration, implementation partners, or support
  • Experience designing or evolving enterprise data architecture, including systems of record, data models, interfaces, contracts, quality, reconciliation, governance, lineage, and downstream consumption
  • Experience partnering with enterprise Data Engineering or Analytics organizations and integrating operational systems with platforms such as Databricks, Snowflake, or similar enterprise data technologies
  • Experience establishing modern engineering practices within enterprise application environments, including automated testing, CI/CD, source control, observability, release management, documentation, and operational readiness
  • Understanding of modern AI capabilities and the ability to identify practical applications of LLMs, agents, and intelligent automation while appropriately managing financial, security, and compliance risk
  • Strong understanding of financial controls, auditability, security, data integrity, and compliance considerations associated with business-critical financial platforms
  • Experience governing system integrators and technology vendors during large transformatio

You will work directly with customer security leaders (security engineers through CISOs) to communicate and clarify product security posture and controls results (such as pen test results), and will work with Smartsheet engineering to build security features that meet real-world customer requirements.  You will display product understanding through highly customized presentation demonstrations to customers and at conferences and events.

  • Ability to explain CI/CD and SDLC best practices and how Smartsheet is deployed.

  • Familiarity with NIST 800-53, ISO, SOC 2, FedRAMP, GDPR, and HIPAA.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels and create external-facing technical content.

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer - Observability & Telemetry Data
jobs.description:
For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Now, in our most ambitious chapter yet, we are uniting human teams with AI agents. By orchestrating the work agents do best, automating manual tasks and uncovering insights at scale, we create the space for people to focus on what truly matters: judgment, creativity, and big thinking. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

Observability Engineering owns the breadth and depth of observability and telemetry at Smartsheet. We build and operate the shared platform every engineering team depends on to understand how their software behaves in production (metrics, logs, distributed traces, RUM, synthetics, and AI/agentic telemetry) across a global, multi-region, commercial and government footprint. We are consolidating ownership of all of it into a single correlated platform, and treating telemetry as what it actually is: one of the largest and most valuable datasets at the company. It's a broad mandate with real scope to shape, and we hold this internal platform to the same rigor, reliability, and product standards as customer-facing software. 

As a Principal Software Engineer (Observability & Telemetry Data), you will set the technical direction for how Smartsheet collects, models, stores, and derives value from telemetry data. This is an architect role: you will define the telemetry data platform and the standards that govern it, carry that architecture across engineering org boundaries, partner with our Data and AI Platform teams on Databricks and MLflow integration, and act as the company's definitive technical voice on observability. You will influence roadmaps you do not own, resolve the hard design trade-offs between fidelity and cost, and raise the technical bar for every engineer instrumenting a service. 

This full-time position reports to the Team Lead, Observability Engineering and can be located in our Bellevue, WA office, or you may work remotely from anywhere in the US where Smartsheet is a registered employer. 

You Will 

  • Architect the Telemetry Data Platform: Own the end-to-end design for how telemetry is landed, modeled, and queried, including open table formats, partitioning and schema evolution strategy, separation of storage and compute, tiered retention, and the query interfaces engineers actually use. Make telemetry a durable, portable, Smartsheet-owned dataset rather than a vendor-locked byproduct. 
  • Own the Telemetry Data Model: Define the semantic conventions, shared business identifiers (user, org, plan, tenant), and schema standards that let any signal be correlated with any other, and drive their adoption across every service team at Smartsheet. 
  • Set OpenTelemetry Direction: Lead the migration to OTel-based instrumentation, defining collector architecture, context propagation, and sampling strategy (including tail-based sampling) so that engineers can move from a log line to a trace to a metric without losing the thread.
  • Integrate AI and Agentic Telemetry with Databricks: Own the architecture connecting our observability platform to Databricks and MLflow, so that agentic and model telemetry (prompt, completion, tool and MCP calls, evaluation results) is captured un-sampled, stays useful under the input/output redaction our governance requires, and reconciles cleanly with the traces and metrics in our primary observability stack. 
  • Instrument the Data Platform Itself: Bring first-class observability to our data estate, including Databricks jobs, pipelines, and warehouses, with meaningful signals for freshness, data quality, lineage, and cost, so data reliability is measured with the same discipline as service reliability. 
  • Build the Analytics Layer on Telemetry: Turn telemetry into decision-grade analytics, covering reliability and incident metrics, telemetry cost and chargeback models, and adoption and coverage reporting that leadership can act on. 
  • Engineer Collection and Routing at Scale: Architect the high-volume collection and routing tier (FluentBit, Kinesis, and OTel collectors) that moves telemetry from every service to its destination across US, EU, AU, and GovCloud regions, and own the migration of these pipelines as we consolidate onto a unified backend. 
  • Own Telemetry Economics: Set the cost architecture for observability data, including ingest governance, cardinality control, and storage tiering, so that teams get the fidelity they need to debug without the spend pressure that causes them to under-instrument. 
  • Carry Architecture Across Org Boundaries: Partner with the Data Platform, AI Platform, and infrastructure organizations to align telemetry architecture with theirs, influence roadmaps you do not own, and represent observability in company-level platform and vendor decisions. 
  • Raise the Technical Bar: Lead design and code reviews, author the architecture decisions and standards others build against, and mentor senior and mid-level engineers on instrumentation, telemetry data modeling, and cost-aware design. 
  • Participate in a production support and on-call rotation, taking ownership of the most complex issue resolution and driving root-cause analysis that improves system resiliency. 

You Have 

  • 10+ years of experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems, data platforms, or observability infrastructure, including time at Principal or Staff level. 
  • Deep Observability Expertise: Hands-on production ownership of metrics, logs, and distributed tracing at scale, including at least one major backend (Datadog, or comparable) and a working understanding of cardinality and cost mechanics. 
  • Telemetry Data Engineering: Demonstrated depth in large-scale data architecture, including open table formats (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg), Spark or comparable distributed processing, streaming ingestion, partitioning and schema evolution, and query performance and cost tuning over very large datasets. 
  • Databricks Depth: Practical experience with the Databricks platform (jobs, clusters, Unity Catalog, Delta) and with MLflow for model and agent telemetry. 
  • OpenTelemetry Depth: Practical experience with OTel collectors, semantic conventions, context propagation, and sampling strategy, including tail-based sampling. 
  • Pipeline Engineering: Experience with high-volume log and telemetry pipelines, including FluentBit or Fluentd, streaming transport such as Kinesis or Kafka, and search backend index and mapping design.
  • Advanced AWS & Kubernetes Expertise: EKS, ECS Fargate, EC2, Lambda, and CloudWatch in production. 
  • 10+ years of programming experience with modern languages such as Go, Java, Python, or Scala, and strong SQL. 
  • Infrastructure as Code: Terraform, and GitOps workflows such as Flux or ArgoCD. 
  • Architectural Influence at Scale: A track record of setting technical direction that multiple teams and organizations adopted, including the written artifacts (architecture decisions, standards, RFCs) that made it durable after you moved on. 
  • Strong incident response instincts, with experience improving mean-time-to-resolution through better instrumentation and better data rather than more heroics. 
  • A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical industry experience.
  • Legally eligible to work in the U.S. on an ongoing basis 

Nice to Have 

  • Experience instrumenting LLM or agentic systems, including OTel GenAI semantic conventions and tracing agent tool-call workflows. 
  • Data reliability engineering practice: freshness, quality, and lineage SLOs for production data pipelines
  • Telemetry cost engineering or FinOps at scale. 
  • Experience in regulated environments (FedRAMP, GovCloud) and designing telemetry that remains useful under redaction. 
  • Prometheus, Grafana, and Alertmanager. 
  • Snowflake, or experience operating across more than one lakehouse or warehouse platform. 
  • Service catalog or internal developer platform work (Backstage or similar).

jobs.title: Technical Risk Manager - Sr. Security Engineer I
jobs.description:
For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Now, in our most ambitious chapter yet, we are uniting human teams with AI agents. By orchestrating the work agents do best, automating manual tasks and uncovering insights at scale, we create the space for people to focus on what truly matters: judgment, creativity, and big thinking. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

Smartsheet needs a clear, defensible answer to "how risky is this?" for the risks that live inside our own environment and the risks that come in through every vendor and partner we rely on. We're looking for a Sr. Security Engineer I to own our Security Risk Management program end-to-end—running risk identification, analysis, and quantification; maintaining the enterprise risk register; and driving mitigation strategies that leadership can act on—while also overseeing our Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) function. You don't need to be a hands-on security engineer to succeed here: you need to understand our technology and architecture well enough to have a real conversation with engineering teams about their risk exposure, and you need the judgment and communication skill to turn technical risk into business language that drives decisions. This role sits at the center of how Smartsheet decides what to fix first, what to accept, and what a vendor relationship is actually costing us in risk.

This role reports to the Senior Director, GRC Engineering and can be based in our Bellevue, WA office or remotely from anywhere in the US where Smartsheet is a registered employer.

You Will:

  • Own and mature Smartsheet's Security Risk Management program: risk identification, analysis, scoring, and quantification (e.g., FAIR-based or similar) across internal systems, third parties, and emerging initiatives.
  • Maintain the enterprise risk register—ratings, ownership, mitigation status, and residual risk—and drive it toward a living, decision-useful tool rather than a static spreadsheet.
  • Lead risk analysis and reviews for new initiatives, architecture changes, and significant findings, translating technical exposure into business-relevant risk statements for leadership.
  • Develop and drive risk mitigation strategy: work with risk owners across engineering, IT, and business teams to define remediation plans, track them to closure, and escalate what isn't moving.
  • Oversee Smartsheet's Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) program: vendor risk tiering, security assessment/questionnaire review, ongoing monitoring, and issue tracking for the vendor and partner ecosystem.
  • Build and present risk reporting and KPIs/KRIs to security and business leadership, giving them a clear view of top enterprise risks and where mitigation investment should go.
  • Partner with GRC, Field Security Engineering, and engineering leads to make sure risk findings from audits, pen tests, and questionnaires feed back into the same risk register and prioritization process.

You Have:

  • 4+ years of experience in security risk management, enterprise risk, or GRC, including direct ownership of a risk register and risk assessment process.
  • Working familiarity with risk quantification approaches (FAIR, OCTAVE, or similar) and the judgment to apply them practically rather than academically.
  • Enough technical fluency to understand cloud architecture, application security concepts, and common vulnerability/risk findings well enough to discuss them credibly with engineering teams—deep hands-on engineering experience is not required.
  • Experience running or closely supporting a Third-Party Risk Management program: vendor tiering, questionnaire review, and ongoing monitoring.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; you can brief a risk finding to an engineering lead and to an executive and have both walk away with the right takeaway.
  • Strong organizational skills and comfort managing many concurrent risk items and vendor relationships without losing track of status.
  • Professional certifications: CRISC, CISSP, CISM, or equivalent.
  • Experience with GRC or TPRM tooling (Vanta, Drata, OneTrust, Archer, ServiceNow GRC, or similar).
  • Background supporting SOC 2, ISO 27001, or FedRAMP programs and an understanding of how risk management ties into those certifications.

This is the most senior individual contributor role on the Application Security team. The expectation is not just depth: it is reach. You will engage product and engineering leadership directly, drive security requirements rather than advisory recommendations, and build team capability over time. If you are a security engineer who thinks upstream, builds threat models that generate concrete test scenarios and can translate technical findings into architecture decisions and business outcomes, this role is built for you.

This role reports to the Manager, Application Security and can be based in our Bellevue, WA office or remotely from anywhere in the US where Smartsheet is a registered employer.

You Will: 

  • Lead Threat Modeling and Product Security Reviews: Own threat modeling and product security review as the team's primary upstream capability: build models from architecture and data-flow artifacts, derive concrete abuse cases and test scenarios, and drive security requirements into designs before they ship. Build runbooks, standards, and documentation that create consistency and reduce single-point-of-failure risk as the team scales.
  • Elevate Team Capability and Engineering Organization Influence: Mentor AppSec team members on threat modeling tradecraft and security review design, and serve as the trusted technical voice with product and engineering leadership, framing risk in terms that move architecture decisions. Your judgment shapes how the team prioritizes and how the broader organization understands and invests in application security.

  • Ability to own threat modeling as a systematic practice (STRIDE, data-flow and architecture diagram driven), producing concrete, actionable test scenarios and abuse cases, embedded into agile design cycles as a repeatable, lightweight practice.
  • Hands-on experience securing AI-integrated applications (LLM workflows, agentic systems, model APIs, MCP-based integrations) with fluency in the OWASP LLM Top 10 and current AI attack classes, plus experience using AI tooling to scale security review coverage.
  • Experience doing architecture review and targeted manual code review for complex SaaS features, with a track record of driving remediation requirements through to implementation with enough technical credibility to influence design decisions at the engineering leadership level.

jobs.title: Analytical Lab Technician
jobs.description:
About Redwood Materials

Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. On the energy side, Redwood has deployed the largest second-life battery project in the world, delivering power to AI data centers in months rather than years using proprietary energy architecture engineered entirely in-house. The company is profitable, the market it operates in is projected to grow 20 to 50 times over the next decade, and Redwood is the only company with the supply chain, the technology, and the operational scale to lead it.

Analytical Laboratory Technician

The Analytical Lab Technician performs routine chemical and laboratory analytical tasks in support of production quality and safety at Redwood Materials facilities. Working under supervision for all assigned tasks, this role is responsible for executing established laboratory procedures per written SOPs and TCMs, accurate sample handling and data entry, basic instrument operation, and adherence to all chemical safety and documentation standards. This role develops foundational proficiency in analytical methods, laboratory information systems, and lab safety while building toward independent operation. 

Shifts: B shift - Sunday -Tuesday 5 pm - 5 am, alternating Wednesdays 
C shift - Sunday-Tuesday 5 am - 5 pm, alternating Wednesday

Responsibilities will include: 

  • Prepares samples for analysis using established tests and techniques.  
  • Assists with and performs routine chemical, metrological, and/or metallurgical analysis and reporting.  
  • Maintains laboratory instrumentation and equipment, including troubleshooting and performing verifications.  
  • Works in a production environment, sampling and testing physical characteristics.  
  • Performs additional duties as required, including lab organization, inventory, safety audits, and special projects.  
  • Works effectively in both team and individual environments. 

Desired Qualifications: 

  • Bachelor’s degree in science or related field or 2+ years of related experience.  
  • Experience in laboratory settings, quality settings, or chemical production facilities.  
  • Experience in typical laboratory practices including waste handling, safe work practices, data entry and management, good documentation practices and experimental setup and execution.  
  • Comfortable wearing personal protective equipment including but not limited to lab coats and respirators.  
  • Experience with relevant test methods such as ICP-OES, auto-titration, X-Ray Fluorescence, Total Organic Carbon, etc.  
  • Experience with sample prep and analysis, chemical handling and laboratory hazards.  
  • Demonstrates ability to perform basic chemistry math and calculations.  
  • Adept with data acquisition and analysis tools including Laboratory Information Management Systems and Microsoft Office.  
  • Excellent written, verbal communication, and collaboration skills  
  • Excellent attitude: understands priorities change with company needs and willing to work to ensure deadlines are met. Ability to execute with a calm and collaborative urgency.  
  • Ability to regularly lift 35 lbs.  
  • Use of a step ladder  
  • Sit and or stand for long periods of time, greater than 2 hours  
  • A passion for sustainability and making the world a better place!  

The position is full-time. Compensation will be commensurate with experience.

jobs.title: Staff Mechanical Design Engineer, Big Machines
jobs.location: McCarran, NV; San Francisco, California, United States
jobs.description:
About Redwood Materials

Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. On the energy side, Redwood has deployed the largest second-life battery project in the world, delivering power to AI data centers in months rather than years using proprietary energy architecture engineered entirely in-house. The company is profitable, the market it operates in is projected to grow 20 to 50 times over the next decade, and Redwood is the only company with the supply chain, the technology, and the operational scale to lead it.

About the team 

Big Machines designs and builds custom equipment for our factories and processing plants. Most of what we make can’t be bought from a vendor, so we figure out how to design, build, and commission it ourselves. The scale is big. A full kiln system may weigh 100+ tons and be over 30m long.  

We are looking for an engineer who has owned machinery from concept through commissioning. You have built things that failed and learned the hard lessons. You work from first principles when there is no precedent to lean on, run your own analysis, and you hold a high standard for detail without losing the ability to execute. 

Responsibilities

  • Own the design, build, and commissioning of low-volume, custom integrated machines

  • Perform engineering hand calculations and finite element analysis to size structures and mechanisms

  • Create detailed models and engineering prints in SolidWorks, including managing large assemblies and drawing packages

  • Collaborate with internal fabrication teams and external vendors to manufacture parts

  • Support machine assembly and testing by performing hands-on commissioning, equipment operation, and floor troubleshooting

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or a related discipline

  • 5+ years of professional experience designing and analyzing mechanical structures, mechanisms, or industrial equipment

  • Advanced proficiency in 3D CAD software such as SolidWorks, NX, CATIA, or Creo

  • Strong understanding and application of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience designing and fabricating welded structures

  • Experience designing and testing mechanical mechanisms

  • Experience managing large CAD assembly models and engineering drawings

  • Experience with Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)

  • Experience integrating servos, actuators, and sensors

  • Hands-on experience working in a production facility with heavy equipment and industrial machinery

In accordance with California pay transparency laws, the salary range for this position is listed below. Actual compensation may vary based on a variety of factors, including experience, education, and skills. 

California Pay Range:
$147,500—$235,000 USD

The position is full-time. Compensation will be commensurate with experience.

 

We collect personal information (PI) from you in connection with your application for employment with Redwood Materials, including the following categories of PI: identifiers, personal records, professional or employment information, and inferences drawn from your PI. We collect your PI for our purposes, including performing services and operations related to your potential employment. If you have additional privacy-related questions, please contact us at privacy@redwoodmaterials.com.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer, T&E
jobs.location: New York, New York, United States
jobs.description:
Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Design at Brex

Design at Brex creates the experiences that make complex systems feel effortless through thoughtful, scalable design. Whether crafting interfaces, shaping product strategy, or harnessing AI to empower our users, we obsess over quality and clarity. This is a team for designers who want to build, not just talk about building. We ship constantly, use AI to move faster, and care deeply about craft. Product designers at Brex partner closely with Product, Engineering, Research, Data, and Go-to-Market teams to solve high-stakes problems for ambitious companies that rely on Brex to run their finances.

What you’ll do

As a Senior Product Designer, you’ll lead ambiguous, cross-functional product work from problem definition through shipped execution. You’ll turn complex financial workflows into clear, intuitive experiences that help customers move faster, make better decisions, and trust the systems they use every day.

You’ll be expected to operate with high ownership and low oversight: identifying what needs to be true, breaking ambiguity into actionable paths, facilitating alignment across partners, and shipping iteratively toward measurable customer and business outcomes. You’ll bring strong craft, product judgment, and systems thinking to the work — raising the quality of both the product experience and the way the team designs.

About the team

The Travel & Expenses design team designs how employees spend, report, and get reimbursed, and how finance teams set and enforce the rules behind it. Our work covers travel booking, expense management, reimbursements, and the policy and compliance tools that sit underneath them.

Most of our customers don’t think about this software until something goes wrong: a receipt is missing, a reimbursement hasn’t arrived, a trip falls outside policy. Our job is to make those moments clear and quick for employees, and to give finance teams the control and visibility they need without adding work for everyone else. We’re also building AI agents that handle the manual parts of expenses and compliance, and we design how those agents behave, explain themselves, and recover when they’re wrong.

Responsibilities

  • Own the design direction for a core area of travel and expenses and set a vision and roadmap for it with Product and Engineering.
  • Take loosely defined problems and decide what needs to be true, what to build first, and what to leave out. Turn them into clear scope, milestones, and shippable increments.
  • Define the underlying models (states, transitions, edge cases) before designing screens, so the product behaves consistently across surfaces, and bring those models to the other teams that depend on them.
  • Plan, run, and synthesize your own research, and use customer feedback and data to make and validate design decisions.
  • Design AI-assisted experiences, including how an agent asks for confirmation, explains what it did, and lets people fix mistakes.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering as an equal on scope, sequencing, and tradeoffs. Raise risks early and keep design involved through build.
  • Work across team boundaries on shared components, policy rules, and payment flows. Resolve conflicts before they reach engineering, and represent design in cross-team planning.
  • Raise the quality bar for the team through critique, clear standards for content, color, and component states, and contributions to the design system.
  • Mentor other designers through feedback, pairing, and sharing how you approach ambiguous problems.
  • Present work and rationale clearly to leadership, partners, and customers, and document decisions so others can build on them.

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our San Francisco, Seattle, or New York City office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work.

Requirements

  • 6+ years of product design experience, with a track record of shipping end-to-end features in fast-paced product teams.
  • Strong portfolio of shipped product work, ideally across complex workflows, systems, or customer-facing business software.
  • Experience independently leading ambiguous product initiatives and turning loosely defined problems into clear, executable plans.
  • Strong product thinking, including the ability to connect design decisions to customer needs, business goals, and measurable outcomes.
  • High craft across UX, interaction design, visual design, prototyping, and systems thinking.
  • Experience partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Research, Data, and other cross-functional partners throughout the product development process.
  • Ability to facilitate discussions, synthesize inputs, communicate tradeoffs, and build alignment across stakeholders.
  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where priorities evolve and designers are expected to bias toward learning, iteration, and shipped impact.
  • Clear communication, strong feedback habits, and a collaborative approach to improving both your own work and the work of others.

Bonus points

  • Experience designing financial products, developer tools, enterprise software, or other complex B2B workflows.
  • Experience using AI tools for prototyping, research synthesis, design exploration, or day-to-day workflow acceleration.
  • Experience contributing to or evolving a design system at scale.
  • Experience conducting or partnering on generative and evaluative research.
  • Strong ability to translate complex product, technical, or business constraints into simple customer experiences.

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $192,000 - $240,000. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

Please be aware, job-seekers may be at risk of targeting by malicious actors looking for personal data. Brex recruiters will only reach out via LinkedIn or email with a brex.com domain. Any outreach claiming to be from Brex via other sources should be ignored.

jobs.title: Supply Chain Manager, Aftermarket Operations
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management. 

We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation, more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.

You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries. 

About the Role

Our team drives global demand and supply planning across all hardware product lines, optimizing forward and reverse inventory across regional warehouses to fulfill customer demand. We keep hardware moving through its full lifecycle. 

As our supply chain continues to evolve with the growing business, we’re looking for a Supply Chain Manager for Aftermarket Operations to own the strategy and outcomes for our products' full post-sale lifecycle — refurbishment, spare parts, end-of-service, and non-revenue inventory. You'll manage key vendor relationships directly, make planning and disposition calls in your areas, and partner closely with engineering and quality teams to support failure analysis on warranty returns.

We are committed to a thriving in-office culture. This role requires that you be on-site at our office in San Mateo, CA 5 days a week.

What You'll Do

  • Refurb Strategy & Vendor Ownership: Own the strategy for which products get refurbished and where, and when to sunset a product from the program. Directly manage our primary refurbishment vendor relationship and own production planning and prioritization across refurb sites to keep throughput aligned with demand.
  • Refurb Quality & Production Oversight: Own quality control standards for refurbished units and drive resolution when quality or output falls short. Partner with internal stakeholders to manage the day-to-day operations. 
  • Spare Parts Program Ownership: Own spare parts strategy end-to-end — from setup and stocking decisions through fulfillment — including the internal and external catalog and ordering experience. Define the spares approach for products approaching or past end-of-service.
  • End-of-Service Strategy: Own the strategy and operational execution for transitioning products through end-of-service, balancing customer impact, cost, and inventory exposure.
  • Non-Revenue Inventory & Disposition: Own the KPIs for non-revenue and returned inventory turnaround, and set the disposition rules that determine how returned inventory gets processed, resold, or retired. Drive fulfillment of non-revenue demand across the business.
  • Warranty Program Support: Serve as the supply chain counterpart to quality and engineering teams on warranty returns — helping stand up and refine triage processes at our refurb center as needs evolve, and ensuring engineering gets the units they need for deeper investigation without delay.

What You Bring

  • Experience: 4+ years in reverse logistics, aftermarket operations, refurbishment, or a closely related supply chain discipline.
  • Vendor & Partner Management: Track record of managing an external operational partner directly — setting expectations, holding performance to standard, and resolving issues in real time.
  • Decision-Making Under Ambiguity: Comfort setting rules and standards (e.g., disposition criteria, quality bars) where no playbook exists yet, and defending those decisions with data.
  • Strategic Ownership: A track record of taking a broad, open-ended mandate from leadership and shaping it into a concrete plan yourself — including bringing your own point of view on the right approach, not just executing steps someone else defined.
  • Cross-Functional Influence: Proven ability to drive outcomes through people who don't report to you — coordinating across warehouse, engineering, quality, and other operational teams to keep shared work moving.
  • Data Fluency: Comfortable defining a KPI, pulling your own data to support a decision, and using data to catch problems before they become escalations.
  • Flexibility to Travel: Willing and able to travel up to 25% of the time domestically and internationally.
  • Must be willing and able to commute 5 days in office.
  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Finance, Data Operations, Business, or a related field.

Employee Benefits

Verkada is committed to fostering a workplace environment that prioritizes the holistic health and wellbeing of our employees and their families by offering comprehensive wellness perks, benefits, and resources. Our benefits and perks programs include, but are not limited to:

  • Healthcare programs that can be tailored to meet the personal health and financial well-being needs - Premiums are 100% covered for the employee under at least one plan and 80% for family premiums under all plans
  • Nationwide medical, vision and dental coverage
  • Starting January 2027, Verkada will match a portion of an employee’s 401(k) contributions based on eligible earnings. Match vests on 2 year anniversary
  • Health Saving Account (HSA) with annual employer contributions and Flexible Spending Account (FSA) with tax saving options
  • Expanded mental health support
  • Paid parental leave policy & fertility benefits
  • Time off to relax and recharge through our paid holidays, firmwide extended holidays, flexible PTO and personal sick time
  • Professional development stipend
  • Wellness/fitness benefits
  • Healthy lunches provided daily
  • Commuter benefits

Additional Information

  • You must be independently authorized to work in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa for this role, at this time.

Annual Pay Range

At Verkada, we want to attract and retain the best employees, and compensate them in a way that appropriately and fairly values their individual contribution to the company. With that in mind, we carefully consider a number of factors to determine the appropriate starting pay for an employee, including their primary work location and an assessment of a candidate's skills and experience, as well as market demands and internal parity. A Verkada employee may be eligible for additional forms of compensation, depending on their role, including sales incentives, discretionary bonuses, and/or equity in the company in the form of restricted stock units (RSUs)

Below is the annual on-target earnings (OTE) range for full-time employees for this position, comprised of base compensation and commissions (if applicable).

Estimated Annual Pay Range
$130,000—$170,000 USD

Verkada Is An Equal Opportunity Employer

As an equal opportunity employer, Verkada is committed to providing employment opportunities to all individuals. All applicants for positions at Verkada will be treated without regard to race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, marital status, veteran status, pregnancy, or any other basis prohibited by applicable law.

Your application will be handled in accordance with our Candidate Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Sr. Client Account Manager, Financial Services
jobs.description:
About Pinterest:

Millions of people around the world come to our platform to find creative ideas, dream about new possibilities and plan for memories that will last a lifetime. At Pinterest, we’re on a mission to bring everyone the inspiration to create a life they love, and that starts with the people behind the product.

Discover a career where you ignite innovation for millions, transform passion into growth opportunities, celebrate each other’s unique experiences and embrace the flexibility to do your best work. Creating a career you love? It’s Possible.

At Pinterest, AI isn't just a feature, it's a powerful partner that augments our creativity and amplifies our impact, and we’re looking for candidates who are excited to be a part of that. To get a complete picture of your experience and abilities, we’ll explore your foundational skills and how you collaborate with AI.

Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process here.

As a Sr. Client Account Manager, you will play a pivotal role in driving business results for Pinterest’s largest strategic advertisers. Your expertise throughout the funnel tactics will help you grow and nurture client relationships and guide them from awareness through to conversion and retention. We’re looking for a Client Account Manager to help our most strategic partners successfully grow their business through Pinterest. You’ll work directly with some of our key advertisers as a trusted consultant to their business. Your strategic advice, analytical skills and sales skills are core to bringing to life the value we deliver as a platform.

In this role, you'll focus on Financial Services advertisers, who rely on a true full-funnel strategy to earn trust, build brand consideration, and ultimately drive high-value actions like account openings, loan originations, and policy sign-ups. Pinterest's unique intent-driven environment is where consumers plan major financial decisions, making you a strategic partner in connecting Financial Services brands with consumers at every stage of that journey. You'll need to balance brand-safety and compliance sensitivities unique to this vertical with a sharp focus on measurable, bottom-line performance

We invite passionate candidates to join our US Enterprise Sales team, where we have open positions across several business sectors, in various locations. By applying for the Sr. Client Account Manager position, your application will be considered for all available roles that match your skills and experience. Submit your resume once, and it will be considered by multiple hiring teams.


What you'll do:

  • Plan, execute, upsell, and optimize data-driven ad campaigns in collaboration with internal teams.
  • Build and maintain strategic partnerships, aligning with stakeholder goals across all funnel stages.
  • Ensure accurate implementation of first-party data and campaign launches with cross-functional teams.
  • Optimize media campaigns and audience targeting daily using various technologies and platforms.
  • Deliver weekly campaign performance reporting and insights.
  • Advise clients on Pinterest ad products, targeting, bidding, creative, and measurement strategies.
  • Provide exceptional client service through communication, issue resolution, and seamless execution.
  • Simplify complex processes, upsell and pitch strategic solutions, and continuously improve campaigns.


What we're looking for:

  • Proven experience managing and growing client accounts with data-driven strategies.
  • Strong knowledge of advertising best practices and technical media measurement.
  • Skilled at identifying client needs, communicating persuasive recommendations, and overcoming objections.
  • Ability to build and execute full-funnel sales strategies, driving adoption and conversions.
  • Excellent at managing multiple campaigns, tasks, and timelines simultaneously.
  • Outstanding verbal and written communication skills with a proactive, problem-solving mindset.
  • Demonstrates curiosity and a willingness to explore AI tools to improve day-to-day productivity, including campaign setup, performance reporting, client communications, and research. Leverages AI to work more efficiently, whether it's streamlining optimizations, preparing for client meetings, or surfacing insights from campaign data, while maintaining attention to detail and a high bar for accuracy.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Sales, or related field, or equivalent experience.


In-Office Requirement Statement:

  • We recognize that the ideal environment for work is situational and may differ across departments. What this looks like day-to-day can vary based on the needs of each organization or role.
  • This role will need to be in the office for in-person collaboration 2 times per week and therefore needs to be in a commutable distance from our New York office.


Relocation Statement:

  • This position is not eligible for relocation assistance. Visit our PinFlex page to learn more about our working model.

#LI-HYBRID 

#LI-KP3
